about: THE WATER OF EVERY LEVEL c. 800 (the user, 4 Oct: each level has to have the exact right and correct water). Merged by hand from Research/water_levels/<region>.json (each record keeps its sources, confidence and notes; numbers marked estimate or guess there are so here). The game reads: tide, river (width, depth, currents low/mean/flood, flood and low months, flood rise, ice), sea, optics (Secchi depth by season, colour, temperature). Regenerate by merging the research files again when they change.

records.name: The western Baltic (Belt Sea, Mecklenburg Bight, Arkona Sea)

tide.phaseNote: The tide is a weak echo of the Kattegat: at most 30 cm at Flensburg, fading to practically nothing in the central Baltic (verified). Water level is driven by wind set-up and the basin seiche, not by the moon. The stream figure is the level-driven outflow and inflow through the Fehmarn Belt and the Sound, not tidal (knowledge).
tide.notes: Storm set-up up to about 2.5 m above mean (verified, de.wikipedia Ostsee); the 13 Nov 1872 surge peaked about 3.3 m above NN (verified). The Baltic's fundamental seiche runs about a day (verified, de.wikipedia Seiche; literature value about 27 h, knowledge): a SW gale pushes the water toward Finland, and when it veers NE the water sloshes back, the 1872 mechanism (verified). Set-down of 1-1.5 m in a long westerly is common (knowledge). Relative sea level c. 800 on the German and Danish south coasts about 0.5 m (0.3-1.0) lower than today (estimate: slow subsidence of the southern Baltic plus the late-Holocene rise, knowledge of Lampe/Harff-type curves).

waves.swellFrom: E and NE (long fetch down the Baltic Proper); otherwise a short steep wind sea
waves.notes: Fetch-limited, short-period, steep: 2 m at 5-6 s feels worse than its height. All Hs values are estimates from the Arkona buoy climate and Baltic hindcasts (knowledge; Tuomi et al. 2011 identified, not opened). Wind against the outflow current steepens and breaks the sea in the Belts.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Brackish surface outflow runs W/NW through the Fehmarn Belt, Great Belt and Sound at 0.2-1 kn, reversing for days in westerly gales (knowledge; the Sound's surface stream 'often northbound' and changing day to day, verified).
sea.notes: In severe winters nearly the whole Baltic freezes as far as Bornholm (verified, de.wikipedia Ostsee). With 793's -0.8 C: drift ice in the Belts and the Mecklenburg Bight about 1 winter in 5-7, a closed Belt about 1 in 15-20 (guess, scaled from the Danish ice-winter record of the cold 17th-19th c., knowledge). After 950 (MCA) fewer.

optics.colour: Cold bottle-green to grey-green, never blue; a green-yellow cast from dissolved organic matter coming out of the Baltic; whitecaps grey-white.
optics.turbidityCause: Phytoplankton (spring and late-summer blooms) and CDOM in the outflow; little mineral silt offshore.

salinityPsu.note: About 15-20 in the Kiel Bight falling to about 8 at Arkona (verified overall range: under 3 in the Bothnian Bay to about 20 in the western Baltic). Sound: 10-12 south, above 20 north of Helsingør (verified). MCA salinity perhaps 1-2 higher (guess, from MCA hypoxia and diatom records, knowledge).

hazards.name: Gedser Rev and the Darss sill
hazards.danger: Shoal ridge of 7-18 m with shallower spits; breaking seas in a NE gale (knowledge).

hazards.name: Fehmarn Belt and Great Belt currents
hazards.where: Fehmarn Belt, Langeland Belt, Great Belt narrows
hazards.danger: Outflow of 1-3 kn against a westerly gale raises a steep breaking sea (knowledge).

hazards.name: Kadetrinne
hazards.danger: Narrow deep channel between boulder shoals (knowledge).

hazards.name: Winter drift ice
hazards.danger: Pack ice can nip or hole a clinker hull; fast ice closes harbours (knowledge).

phenomena: Seiche-driven level swings of 0.5-1.5 m over a day with no wind on the spot
Storm set-up of 1.5-2.5 m in a NE gale after a SW gale (the 1872 pattern)
Short steep chop, breaking crests from Bft 5
Glassy summer calms with cat's paws; looming and heat shimmer over cool water
Sea fog in spring and early summer (warm air over cold water)
Late-summer cyanobacteria streaks on calm days, fewer than today
Drift ice and frost smoke (sea smoke) in hard winters
records.change_800_to_1066: Little physical change. Relative sea level crept up a few decimetres on the German coast (estimate). The MCA from about 950 brings milder winters, fewer ice winters and perhaps slightly saltier surface water (guess). The 1044 storm flood is the first recorded Baltic surge on this coast (knowledge, not verified this session).
records.then_vs_now: No dredged channels, moles, breakwaters, Kiel Canal, bridges or dikes; coasts eroding freely; sea about 0.5 m lower; water clearer (pre-eutrophication Secchi probably 2-3 m more than today, knowledge); colder winters with more ice.

sources.licence_or_note: Facts cited; CC BY-SA text not copied

records.name: Roskilde fjord and Lejre vig

tide.phaseNote: Tide negligible: the Kattegat tide decays through the Isefjord mouth (knowledge). Level follows Kattegat set-up, +/-0.5-1 m in storms (estimate).
tide.notes: Shoal margins and reed flats fall dry when an easterly or southerly gale drains the Kattegat (knowledge). Fjord seiche about 3.3 h (estimate: Merian T = 2L/sqrt(gh), L 41.6 km, h 5 m).

waves.swellFrom: none (Kattegat swell does not pass the Isefjord mouth)
waves.notes: Short chop only; the long north-south reach builds about 1 m in a northerly gale (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak; 0.5-1 kn through the narrows at Frederikssund and Skuldelev while the level is changing (estimate).
sea.notes: 41.6 km long, about 5 m deep most places, Hestehullet 29 m (verified, da.wikipedia). Shallow, so it freezes readily: fast ice about every other winter in 793's climate (guess, from modern Danish fjord ice of roughly 1 in 3-4 and -0.8 C).

optics.colour: Pale green over sand and eelgrass in the shallows, darker olive in the channel.
optics.turbidityCause: Phytoplankton and wind-resuspended mud; eelgrass keeps the shallows clear.

salinityPsu.note: Kattegat water diluted by streams; about 12-16 in the north, lower toward Roskilde (estimate).

hazards.name: The Skuldelev narrows (Peberrenden)
hazards.danger: Narrow winding channel between shoals; about AD 1000 ships were sunk here as a blockade (verified c. 1000, en.wikipedia), so later only one way through.

hazards.name: Shoals and holms
hazards.danger: Many low islands and stony shoals; long detours (verified, da.wikipedia).

phenomena: Glassy mornings mirroring the low wooded shores
Eelgrass meadows visible through clear shallow water
Fast ice and skating ice in hard winters
Flats at the fjord head drying in an offshore gale
Mist on cold calm autumn mornings
Fjord seiche of a few cm over about 3 h
records.change_800_to_1066: Hróiskelda grows into a town from about 980 (levels file); the Skuldelev blockade narrows the passage to one channel. Sea level effectively stable (Zealand lies near the uplift hinge line, knowledge).
records.then_vs_now: No modern harbours or dredged channel; the fjord head at Roskilde wetter and reedier; Hleiðr (Lejre) reached by a short walk inland from Lejre vig.

records.name: Lake Tissø

tide.phaseNote: Freshwater lake 2.0 m above DNN (verified).
tide.notes: Seasonal level change of a few decimetres (estimate). Seiche about 0.5 h (estimate, Merian with L 6 km, h 8 m).

river.name: Halleby Å (outflow to the Great Belt)
river.notes: All Halleby Å numbers are estimates (catchment 417.89 km2, verified, times Danish runoff of about 6 l/s/km2, knowledge). A small-boat stream at best: the seat was reached overland from the Great Belt shore about 8 km west, or by small craft up the Å (estimate).

optics.colour: Green-brown lowland lake; dark under wooded shores.
optics.turbidityCause: Summer phytoplankton; little silt.

hazards.name: Thin ice
hazards.danger: Freezes most winters c. 800 (estimate).

phenomena: Mirror-calm mornings
Reed beds and lily pads
Hoar frost on reeds, skating ice
Wind ripple fields running down the length of the lake
records.change_800_to_1066: The Kalmargården magnate seat on the west shore grew from about 18,000 m2 around 900 to about 25,000 m2 around 1000 (verified); it ends about 1030 (levels file).
records.then_vs_now: Area 1,233 ha, mean depth 8.2 m, max 13.5 m today (verified). The level may have stood somewhat higher before modern drainage of the outflow (guess; the source does not say).

records.name: Odense fjord and the Odense river

tide.phaseNote: Small Kattegat tide of 0.2-0.3 m at the fjord mouth (estimate from Danish Belt tide gauges, knowledge); wind set-up dominates.
tide.tidalLimit: No tide felt in the river; set-up backs up a few km (estimate).
tide.notes: The fjord is about 13 km long (verified) and very shallow, much of it 1-2 m (knowledge); Odense lies a few km up the river from the fjord head (estimate).

river.name: Odense Å
river.notes: Discharge and width are estimates (catchment about 1,050 km2 times about 9 l/s/km2, knowledge). Only small boats reached the town; ships lay in the fjord and lightered (estimate).

waves.notes: Sheltered chop.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak.
sea.notes: Two inhabited islands and about 25 holms (verified).

optics.colour: Green-brown and shallow, the sandy bottom showing through.
optics.turbidityCause: Wind-resuspended sand and mud; river silt in flood.

salinityPsu.note: 15-18 at the mouth to near fresh in the river (estimate).

hazards.name: Fjord shoals
hazards.danger: Grounding at set-down; a westerly gale can drop the level about 0.5 m (estimate).

phenomena: Wide shallow mirror at calm
Eelgrass and wading birds
Ice in hard winters
records.change_800_to_1066: Óðinsvé appears as a town from 988 (levels file). Physical change minor.
records.then_vs_now: No dredged ship canal (the Odense canal is 19th century, knowledge); the southern shallows were wider marsh.

records.name: The Schlei to Hedeby (Haddebyer Noor)

tide.phaseNote: The Flensburg-Kiel tide of 0.1-0.3 m (verified: at most 30 cm at Flensburg) is damped along the narrow Schlei; at Hedeby practically nothing. Level follows Kiel Bight set-up and the Baltic seiche.
tide.notes: Storm set-up reaches Schleswig almost in full (the 1872 surge flooded the Schlei shores; Maasholm high-water mark, verified photo caption). Inner Schlei seiche about 4 h (estimate, Merian L 42 km, h 3 m). The narrows (Missunde; Stexwiger Enge 280 m wide, verified) run 1-1.5 kn while the level changes (estimate).

waves.notes: Sheltered; the Große Breite (up to 4.2 km wide, verified) builds a short chop.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Mean outflow small (local streams); level-driven currents dominate in the narrows.
sea.notes: 42 km from Schleimünde to Schleswig, mean width 1.3 km, mean depth 3 m, 54.6 km2 (verified). Max depth is a knowledge value. Fast ice about every other winter c. 800 (estimate: shallow brackish water freezing at about -0.3 C).

optics.colour: Olive-green brackish water; brown over the mud of the inner Noore.
optics.turbidityCause: Phytoplankton and resuspended mud; eutrophic today with dense summer phytoplankton (verified); c. 800 clearer (estimate: Secchi roughly doubled).

salinityPsu.note: 12-20 at Schleimünde falling to 4-8 at Schleswig (verified as 1.2-2.0% and 0.4-0.8%).

hazards.name: Schleimünde bar
hazards.danger: Shifting sand mouth that has moved since the Viking Age (knowledge, not verified); breaking sea on the bar in an easterly.

hazards.name: Stake barriers and sunken ships
hazards.where: Across the Schlei near Reesholm and in front of Hedeby harbour
hazards.danger: Underwater stake barriers of the 8th-11th c. (knowledge); a pilot is needed.

hazards.name: Missunde narrows
hazards.danger: 1-1.5 kn on level changes (estimate).

phenomena: Long glassy reaches between low moraine banks
Reed edges and cattle grazing to the water
Mist rising off the Noore at dawn
Ice in hard winters with sledge traffic
Town smoke lying flat over a calm harbour
Schlei seiche of a few cm over about 4 h
records.change_800_to_1066: Hedeby's jetties push further into the harbour through the 9th-10th c. (knowledge); the town is sacked in 1050 and 1066 and people move across the Schlei to Schleswig (verified). The harbour shoals with refuse and stakes (knowledge).
records.then_vs_now: Not the eutrophic green of today; sea level about 0.5 m lower (estimate as O4); the Haddebyer Noor open to the harbour, not cut off by the modern road dam (knowledge). The portage to the Treene is under 15 km (verified).

records.name: The Sound (Øresund) off Lomma bay and the Lödde å

tide.phaseNote: Daily tides exist but have minimal effect (verified). The stream is the outflow/inflow driven by the level difference between Kattegat and Baltic and can change from one day to the next (verified).
tide.notes: Southern Sound only 5-6 m deep outside the Drogden and Flinten channels (verified). Löddeköpinge sits on the Lödde å a few km from its mouth (estimate). Uppåkra and Lund lie inland (levels file): reached on foot from the landing.

river.name: Lödde å (Kävlinge å)
river.notes: All Lödde å numbers are estimates (catchment about 1,200 km2, Skåne runoff about 8 l/s/km2, knowledge). Navigable for small ships to the köping only.

waves.notes: Fetch-limited; wind against the current in the narrows makes a short breaking sea (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Surface current often northbound out of the Baltic at 0.5-3 kn, reversing in westerly gales (direction verified; speeds knowledge).
sea.notes: 118 km long, 4-28 km wide, about 40 m at the deepest (verified). The Sound froze across in severe winters (1658, knowledge).

optics.colour: Grey-green, with visible lines where brackish surface water rides over saltier water.
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton; otherwise clear.

salinityPsu.note: 10-12 in the south, above 20 north of Helsingør, above 30 below 5-15 m (verified).

hazards.name: Saltholm and Drogden shoals
hazards.danger: 5-6 m and less outside the channels (verified); boulders.

hazards.name: Wind-against-current seas
hazards.danger: Steep breaking seas when 2-3 kn of outflow meets a NW gale (estimate).

phenomena: Current lines and foam streaks along the brackish front
Herring shoals with gulls over them in autumn
Summer sea fog
Drift ice in hard winters
records.change_800_to_1066: Lund replaces Uppåkra about 990 and Löddeköpinge's market ends about 1000 (levels file). Water unchanged.
records.then_vs_now: No bridge, no dredged Drogden channel, no moles; Skåne near the uplift hinge line, so sea level within about +/-0.3 m of today (estimate).

records.name: Hanö bay and the Helge å mouth at Åhus

tide.phaseNote: No tide to speak of (verified: practically none in the central Baltic). Level moves with Baltic set-up and seiche, +/-0.5-1 m (estimate).
tide.tidalLimit: No tide; an easterly set-up backs up the lower river a few km (estimate).
tide.notes: The Helge å reached the sea at Åhus until the 18th-century diversion to Gropahålet (verified: originally at Åhus; sv.wikipedia gives 1785).

river.name: Helge å
river.notes: Mean about 46 m3/s with large natural swings, 0.1 km wide at the mouth, brown humic water (verified). Low and flood flows, depth and speeds are estimates.

waves.notes: Open to the Bornholm basin; surf on the sand beach in an easterly (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak coastal drift.
sea.notes: Long sandy bay shore; the river plume shows as a brown tongue.

optics.colour: Bay grey-green; river tea-brown humic water (verified), with a sharp brown plume edge off the mouth.
optics.turbidityCause: Humic substances from forest and bog (verified); plankton in the bay.

salinityPsu.note: Bay about 7-8 (knowledge, Bornholm basin surface); river fresh.

hazards.name: Mouth bar
hazards.danger: Shifting sand bar; breaking in an easterly (estimate).

phenomena: Brown river plume against green sea
Low sandy beach with surf
River ice floes going out in spring
records.change_800_to_1066: Little change; Áhús a market throughout (levels file).
records.then_vs_now: The river mouth at Åhus itself (no 18th-c. diversion); no modern harbour.

records.name: Bornholm's coasts

tide.phaseNote: No real tide (verified for the central Baltic). Level +/-0.5 m with set-up (estimate).
tide.notes: Sorte Muld lies inland near Svaneke (levels file); landing on the east-coast beaches and coves.

waves.notes: Exposed mid-Baltic island: the first place in O4 with long fetch on all sides. Estimates from the Baltic Proper climate (knowledge).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak, 0.2-0.5 kn and wind-driven; stronger round Hammeren (estimate).
sea.notes: Bornholm basin to about 100 m (knowledge). Granite cliffs north and east, sand in the south.

optics.colour: Clear green-grey over granite and sand; dark blue-green offshore.
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton only.

hazards.name: Hammeren and the north cliffs
hazards.danger: Granite cliffs and reefs with a confused sea in a NE or SW gale (knowledge).

hazards.name: Rønne Banke and Adlergrund
hazards.danger: Shoals of about 6-15 m with breaking seas in storms (knowledge).

hazards.name: Ertholmene reefs
hazards.danger: Rocks in open water (knowledge).

phenomena: Clear water over pink granite
Surf bursting on the cliffs
Sea fog banks drifting over the island in early summer
Seals on the Ertholmene
records.change_800_to_1066: None of note.
records.then_vs_now: No harbour moles; otherwise much as now, water clearer before modern eutrophication. Winter 0-5 C, summer 15-20 C today in the Bornholm basin (verified); 793 a little colder.

records.name: The Bay of Lübeck and the lower Trave to Liubice

tide.phaseNote: Negligible tide (O4); the lower Trave follows the Bay of Lübeck's level, which swings with set-up and seiche.
tide.tidalLimit: No tide; Baltic surges reach Lübeck (verified: the 1872 storm flood hit Lübeck) and so Alt Lübeck, about 20 km up (estimate).
tide.notes: Today a regular inflow of bay water makes the lower Trave brackish at 2-5 g/kg (verified); c. 800, with a natural channel of perhaps 2-4 m instead of the dredged 8.5-9.5 m (verified: dredged from 4 m in 1854 to 9.5 m in 1982), much less salt got in (estimate: under 2).

river.name: Trave (with the Schwartau at Alt Lübeck)
river.notes: Mean 7.9 m3/s at Lübeck-Moisling (verified, 2004-2021). Width, depth, low/flood flows and speeds are estimates. Current reverses when the bay rises.

waves.notes: Fetch-limited; NE gales pile water and waves into the bay corner (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak.
sea.notes: The bay corner gets the highest surge levels on the German coast (the 1872 peak of about 3.3 m was on this coast; verified overall).

optics.colour: River olive-brown; bay grey-green.
optics.turbidityCause: Marsh humics and mud in the river; plankton in the bay.

salinityPsu.note: Bay about 10-14 (estimate); lower Trave c. 800 near fresh except in surges (estimate); today 2-5 (verified).

hazards.name: Storm surge in the bay corner
hazards.danger: Rises of 2-3 m in a NE storm after a SW blow flood the low banks (verified 1872 mechanism).

hazards.name: Shallow natural channel
hazards.danger: Probably 2-4 m in the channel, less on the bends (estimate).

phenomena: Current reversal on a rising bay
Reed marsh and alder carr along the river
Ice in hard winters
records.change_800_to_1066: Liubice (Alt Lübeck) is a fort from 819 (levels file); water unchanged.
records.then_vs_now: No dredged ship channel, no Elbe-Lübeck canal, no moles at Travemünde; much fresher river.

records.name: The Oldenburg graben inlet to Starigard

tide.phaseNote: No tide felt; level follows the Hohwacht bay / Fehmarn Belt set-up (estimate).
tide.notes: Over a thousand years ago the Oldenburger Graben served Oldenburg's defence and was navigable (verified). Today it is a 22 km drainage channel 2-20 m wide, kept 1.6-1.9 m below sea level by pumping (verified). c. 800 it was a shallow brackish inlet or lagoon chain (Gruber See, Wesseker See, verified as natural lakes drained from 1861 on) reaching from the sea toward Starigard (estimate, reconstruction; depth 1-2 m in the channel, guess).

waves.notes: Sheltered marsh water.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak level-driven in- and outflow (estimate).
sea.notes: Shallow brackish-to-fresh water: freezes nearly every winter c. 800 (estimate).

optics.colour: Peaty brown-green marsh water among reeds.
optics.turbidityCause: Peat humics, mud.

salinityPsu.note: Brackish at the sea ends, fresh inland (guess).

hazards.name: Mud shoals and reeds
hazards.danger: Very shallow; only small or light craft (estimate).

phenomena: Reed channels opening into small lakes
Waterbirds rising in clouds
Mist over the marsh at dawn
records.change_800_to_1066: Progressive silting and reed growth; the inlet less usable through the period (guess). Starigard remains the Wagrian seat (levels file).
records.then_vs_now: Today drained and pumped polder 1.6-1.9 m below sea level (verified); then open water and marsh.

records.name: Wismar bay to Reric

tide.phaseNote: Negligible tide; level set by the western Baltic set-up and seiche (O4).
tide.notes: Reric at Groß Strömkendorf lies on the bay's west shore opposite Poel (levels file). Sea level c. 800 about 0.5 m lower than today (estimate, as O4); beach landing, no quays.

waves.notes: Poel and the Salzhaff spits shelter the inner bay (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak.
sea.notes: No numbers found on the page opened (de.wikipedia Wismarbucht has none); depths are estimates from charts (knowledge).

optics.colour: Light green over sand, grey-green deeper.
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton; resuspended sand.

hazards.name: Lieps and Hannibal shoals
hazards.danger: Sand shoals of a few metres (knowledge).

phenomena: Shallow sandy bay, wading birds
Calm glassy water in the lee of Poel
Ice in hard winters
records.change_800_to_1066: Reric is destroyed by the Danish king Godfred in 808 and its merchants moved to Hedeby (knowledge; levels file ends Reric in 808).
records.then_vs_now: No town of Wismar (13th c.), no harbour works; slightly lower sea.

records.name: The Großer Jasmunder Bodden to Ralswiek

tide.phaseNote: No tide; Baltic set-up arrives damped and delayed through the narrow sounds (estimate).
tide.notes: Connected west at the Wittower Fähre to the Rassower Strom and the sea (verified). Bodden seiche about 1-2 h (estimate, Merian L 10 km, h 4 m).

waves.notes: Short chop.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak, through the Wittow narrows on level changes.
sea.notes: 58.4 km2, up to 7 m deep, nearly the whole shore reed-fringed (verified).

optics.colour: Olive-green bodden water, brownish in the reed margins.
optics.turbidityCause: Phytoplankton and resuspended mud.

hazards.name: Wittow narrows
hazards.danger: Narrow shallow passage (knowledge).

phenomena: Reed-girt glassy bodden at dawn
Ice most winters
Mist banks over the water
records.change_800_to_1066: Ralswiek's harbour basin is used through the 9th-10th c. (knowledge).
records.then_vs_now: No 1869 dam at Lietzow (verified), so the Kleiner Jasmunder Bodden was joined; sea level slightly lower (estimate).

records.name: Rügen's outer coast at Cape Arkona

tide.phaseNote: No tide; set-up and seiche as O4.
tide.notes: Chalk and till cliffs; landing in the lee of the cape depending on the wind.

waves.notes: Exposed to the Arkona sea; confused sea off the cape where waves wrap round (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Wind-driven coastal current, accelerating round the cape to about 1 kn (estimate).
sea.notes: Cliff-foot boulder fields; the cliffs erode about decimetres a year (knowledge), so the 800 coast stood some tens of metres further out (estimate).

optics.colour: Milky green near the chalk cliffs (chalk silt), green-grey offshore.
optics.turbidityCause: Chalk and till from cliff erosion near shore.

hazards.name: Cliff-foot boulders and reefs
hazards.danger: Boulder fields from eroded till (knowledge).

phenomena: Chalk-milky water at the cliff foot
Surf in a NE wind
Sea fog in spring
records.change_800_to_1066: The fort and temple of Arkona (from 900 in the levels file); cliff retreat continues.
records.then_vs_now: Cliffs tens of metres further seaward (estimate); no harbour at Vitt.

records.name: The lower Peene to Menzlin

tide.phaseNote: No tide. Several times a year Baltic high water reverses the current (verified), often with reverse flows above the mean discharge at Anklam (verified).
tide.tidalLimit: Backwater from the Baltic reaches far up a river with almost no fall (bed gradient given as 0.25 per mille, verified; the lower river is flatter still, knowledge); reversal at Menzlin several times a year (estimate).
tide.notes: Menzlin lies just above Anklam on the Peene (levels file), about 10 km from the Peenestrom.

river.name: Peene
river.notes: Mean 21.7 m3/s at Anklam, depth 5 m near Anklam (verified, modern). The lower valley is Central Europe's largest continuous fen (verified). Width, speeds and flood flow are estimates; the gradient figure for the lower river is an estimate below the source's 0.25 per mille average.

optics.colour: Dark tea-brown fen water, almost black in shade; reflections like a mirror.
optics.turbidityCause: Peat humics (fen drainage).

hazards.name: Floating fen edges
hazards.danger: No firm bank to land on outside the sand islands (estimate).

phenomena: Black mirror water, almost no visible current
Flow reversal: floating weed drifting upstream
Reed and sedge fen to the horizon
Mosquito clouds in summer, mist in autumn
Ice every winter
records.change_800_to_1066: Menzlin's market ends about 950 (levels file); the fen unchanged.
records.then_vs_now: No dikes, polders or drained fen (the modern valley was drained and partly re-wetted); no Anklam town.

records.name: The Szczecin lagoon, the Dziwna and the Oder mouth

tide.phaseNote: No tide; northerly winds can reverse the flow in the Świna and bring Baltic water into the lagoon (verified).
tide.tidalLimit: Baltic level changes back up the Oder to Szczecin and beyond (estimate).
tide.notes: Outflow shares Peenestrom 17%, Świna 69%, Dziwna 14% today (verified); Wolin sits on the Dziwna. The Świna's dominance is partly modern (dredged channel); c. 800 the Dziwna may have carried more (guess). Lagoon seiche about 4-5 h (estimate, Merian L 50 km, h 3.8 m).

river.name: Oder (Odra) at Szczecin
features: many branches and islands below Gartz
river.notes: Mean 540-567 m3/s (verified: 17 km3/yr, 540 m3/s in the lagoon article; 567 in the Oder article). Low, flood, width, depth and speeds are estimates. Ice jams on the lower Oder in spring (knowledge).

waves.notes: Shallow lagoon chop, steep and short in a westerly (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Net outflow of the Oder; residence time about 55 days (verified).
sea.notes: 687 km2, natural mean depth 3.8 m, max 8.5 m (verified).

optics.colour: Today pea-green hypertrophic (verified); c. 800 a less eutrophic green-brown with river silt (estimate).
optics.turbidityCause: Oder silt and phytoplankton.

salinityPsu.note: 0.5-2 on average, up to 6 when the Świna reverses (verified).

hazards.name: Lagoon shoals
hazards.danger: Shallow sand and mud; the Dziwna is narrow and winding (knowledge).

hazards.name: Ice and ice jams
hazards.danger: Ice every winter; spring jams on the Oder (knowledge).

phenomena: Flat green lagoon with a low horizon
Reed islands and waterbird flocks
Brackish tongues entering through the mouths in a northerly
Summer algal streaks on calm days
Ice every winter
records.change_800_to_1066: Wolin grows into the great emporium of the 10th-11th c. and Szczecin into a fort-town (levels file). The lagoon itself changes little.
records.then_vs_now: No dredged Świna channel or Piastowski canal (19th c., knowledge), no moles at Świnoujście; the lagoon less eutrophic; Oder without its 18th-20th c. straightening.

records.name: The Parsęta mouth and the coast at Kołobrzeg

tide.phaseNote: No tide; Baltic set-up +/-1 m in storms (estimate).
tide.tidalLimit: Set-up backs up the lower Parsęta to Budzistowo, about 3-4 km inland (estimate).
tide.notes: Budzistowo (old Kołobrzeg) lies a few km up the Parsęta; salt springs nearby (knowledge).

river.name: Parsęta
river.notes: All Parsęta numbers are estimates (knowledge: catchment about 3,000 km2).

waves.notes: Open surf coast with offshore bars; boats land in the river mouth (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Eastward longshore drift (knowledge).
sea.notes: Straight sandy coast with two or three breaker bars (knowledge).

optics.colour: Sandy-green surf zone, brown river plume.
optics.turbidityCause: Sand in the surf, river humics.

hazards.name: River-mouth bar and breaker bars
hazards.danger: Breaking seas on the bar in a northerly (estimate).

phenomena: Long lines of surf on bars
Brown river plume
Ice floes on the shore in hard winters
records.change_800_to_1066: A fort from 850; the bishopric 1000 (knowledge).
records.then_vs_now: No moles or port; a river-mouth landing.

records.name: The central Baltic (Bornholm-Gotland basins, northern Baltic Proper)

tide.phaseNote: Tide practically vanishes in the central Baltic (verified).
tide.notes: Level follows the whole-basin seiche (about a day, verified) and wind set-up; coastal levels move +/-0.5-1 m (estimate). Relative sea level c. 800: near today in the south, about 1.5-2.5 m higher on Gotland, about 5 m higher at Stockholm (verified for Mälaren), about 5-6 m higher on Åland (estimate from uplift of about 5 mm/yr, knowledge).

waves.swellFrom: SW (longest fetch), also N in the northern Baltic Proper
waves.notes: Record: Hs 8.2 m with a single wave of 14 m, 22 Dec 2004 (Storm Rafael), northern Baltic Proper; Hs 8.0 m, Jan 2017; highest modelled Hs 9.5 m (verified, FMI). Mean and 99th percentile are estimates (knowledge of Baltic hindcasts). For decision 4 (full height): a full storm sea here is Hs 6-8 m at Tp 10-12 s, steeper than an ocean sea of the same height.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak cyclonic surface circulation, 0.1-0.3 kn, overwhelmed by wind drift (knowledge).
sea.notes: Mean depth of the Baltic Proper 62 m, max 459 m (Landsort Deep) (verified). Ice: about 45% of the Baltic is ice-covered at the average annual maximum (verified, mostly the gulfs); the open central basins freeze only in extreme winters (guess, 1 in 20-30 for 793's climate). Coastal archipelagos (Stockholm, Åland, eastern Gotland harbours) freeze most winters.

optics.colour: Dark green-grey, olive in the sun; a 'Baltic green' from yellow substance, never ocean blue.
optics.turbidityCause: Phytoplankton blooms (spring diatoms, late-summer cyanobacteria) and high CDOM.

salinityPsu.note: About 7-8 in the Bornholm and Gotland basins, 6-7 in the northern Baltic Proper (knowledge). The MCA may have been 1-2 saltier (guess).

hazards.name: Hoburgen and the Gotland reefs
hazards.danger: Limestone reefs, confused sea (knowledge).

hazards.name: Middle Bank and Hoburg Bank
hazards.danger: Open-sea shoals of about 10-20 m with breaking seas in a gale (knowledge).

hazards.name: Storm sea
hazards.danger: Hs 6-8 m in winter storms (verified records).

phenomena: Long low swell after a SW gale
Steep breaking sea in an autumn storm, foam streaks
Glassy summer calms of several days
Late-summer cyanobacteria surface streaks (natural, older than farming, knowledge)
Advection fog in spring
Mirage and looming of islands in calm cold air
records.change_800_to_1066: Uplift continues (about 0.4-0.5 m at Stockholm over the period, from the 5 m since the end of the Viking Age, verified); the MCA warms the water after 950. Otherwise the same sea.
records.then_vs_now: Clearer water: summer Secchi probably 8-9 m before the 20th-century decline (knowledge of the early-1900s Secchi record); no anoxic algal mats ashore; colder winters.

sources.title: FMI, Wave height records in the Baltic Sea

records.name: Gotland's west coast (Paviken, Fröjel, Visby)

tide.phaseNote: No tide (verified, central Baltic).
tide.notes: Paviken was a lagoon-like inlet joined to the sea by a narrow sound, a harbour from the 700s to about 1000, when it silted (verified); land uplift and later drainage filled it (verified). Relative sea level c. 800 about 1.5-2.5 m higher than today (estimate: Gotland uplift of roughly 1-2 mm/yr, knowledge); Fröjel's Viking-age shore lay inland of today's (knowledge).

waves.notes: A lee shore in westerlies; harbours are lagoons and river mouths (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak, wind-driven.
sea.notes: Limestone shore with shingle beaches (raukar further north). Visby's Almedalen was a shallow bay harbour (knowledge).

optics.colour: Very clear over white limestone shingle: pale green inshore, deep green offshore.
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton only; carbonate shore.

hazards.name: Shingle reefs and limestone ledges
hazards.danger: Shallow ledges a few hundred metres out (knowledge).

phenomena: Very clear water over pale stone
Shingle beaches rattling in the swash
Lagoon harbour behind a narrow sound
Glassy evening calm with the sun setting over the sea
records.change_800_to_1066: Paviken silts about 1000 and trade moves to Västergarn (verified); Visby grows from 900 (levels file). Shorelines creep seaward by roughly 0.3-0.5 m of uplift over the period (estimate).
records.then_vs_now: Shore 1.5-2.5 m higher; Paviken an open lagoon harbour not a reed lake of 0.27 km2 (verified for today).

records.name: Kalmar sound off Köpingsvik

tide.phaseNote: No tide; level-driven currents of up to about 1 kn in the narrows (estimate).
tide.notes: Narrowest about 3 km between Öland and the mainland (verified). Köpingsvik is a shallow bay on Öland's west coast (levels file). Uplift small, under 1 m since 800 (estimate).

waves.swellFrom: N or S along the sound
waves.notes: The sound funnels north and south winds (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Up to about 1 kn along the sound with set-up differences (estimate).
sea.notes: Many shoals in the narrows (lighthouses Utgrunden, Garpen named by sv.wikipedia, verified).

optics.colour: Pale green over limestone and sand.
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton.

hazards.name: Utgrunden and Garpen shoals
hazards.danger: Shoals and stones in the fairway (verified names, depths unknown).

phenomena: Funnelled wind and steep chop
Ice in the narrows most winters
Clear shallow water over limestone
records.change_800_to_1066: None of note.
records.then_vs_now: No bridge, no Kalmar castle (12th c.).

records.name: The Mälaren bay of the Baltic (Birka, Helgö, Sigtuna)

tide.phaseNote: No tide. In the Viking Age Mälaren was still a bay of the Baltic (verified), so Baltic set-up and the day-long seiche reached in through the sounds at Stockholm and Södertälje, damped (estimate). Today Mälaren stands 0.7 m above the sea (verified).
tide.notes: Water level at the end of the Viking Age about 5 m above today's (verified, sv.wikipedia Mälaren; the shore at Björkö raised about 5 m, verified). So c. 800: about 5.5 m higher (estimate, uplift of about 4-5 mm/yr). Separation from the Baltic came gradually around the 1000s; by about 1200 the Södertälje and Riddarfjärden entrances were so shallow ships had to unload there (verified). Björkö was much smaller then (verified).

waves.notes: Archipelago lake-bay: short chop on the open fjärdar (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: The outflow of the Mälaren catchment (about 160 m3/s, knowledge) runs out through the eastern sounds at 0.5-1.5 kn in the narrows, reversing when the Baltic is high (estimate).
sea.notes: Today 1,140 km2, mean depth 13 m, max 64-66 m (verified; the 5 m higher stand c. 800 made it larger and deeper). Freezes every winter (knowledge; certain for 793's climate). Winter ice roads were the main winter traffic (knowledge).

optics.colour: Brown-green humic lake-bay water, darker than the open Baltic; tea-coloured in the shallows.
optics.turbidityCause: Humic substances from forest and mire catchments, clay turbidity in the western basins, plankton.

salinityPsu.note: Estimate with reasoning: Baltic surface water off Stockholm is about 5-6 (knowledge); a 5 m higher sea made the inlets wide and deep enough for salt to enter in easterly set-up, but the catchment outflow of about 160 m3/s through the sounds keeps the surface layer fresh most of the time. So: eastern Mälaren near Birka 0.5-2 (guess), fresh in the western basins, brackish pulses after Baltic high water, possibly a salty bottom layer in the deeps. By 1066 effectively fresh.

hazards.name: Skerries and stone shoals
hazards.danger: Glacially smoothed rocks just awash; many uncharted (knowledge).

hazards.name: Ice
hazards.danger: Closes navigation every winter, roughly Dec-Apr in 793's climate (estimate).

phenomena: Glassy mornings among wooded islands
Mist on the fjärdar at dawn in autumn
Black ice and ice roads in winter
Ice break-up drift in April
Cat's paws racing across from the gaps between islands
records.change_800_to_1066: About 0.5 m of uplift over the period (estimate); the sounds shoal; Birka is abandoned about 960-975 (verified and levels file) and Sigtuna takes over from about 980. Salinity, never high, falls to fresh.
records.then_vs_now: Water about 5 m higher than today, so islands smaller, sounds wider, many of today's fields and meadows water; no Stockholm (founded 13th c.), no locks or regulation. A bay of the sea, not a lake.

records.name: The Ekoln bay and the Fyris river to Uppsala

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.tidalLimit: Baltic level reached into Ekoln when Mälaren was a bay (estimate).
tide.notes: With water about 5.5-6.5 m higher c. 800 (estimate: Uppsala uplift slightly above Stockholm's, knowledge), the Ekoln bay reached to about the southern edge of today's Uppsala (estimate); Gamla Uppsala lies about 5 km further north up the Fyris.

river.name: Fyrisån
features: the 4 m fall at Ulva mill upstream of Gamla Uppsala
river.notes: Mean 10 m3/s at Uppsala, 14 at the mouth; a 4 m fall at Ulva kvarn (verified). Other numbers are estimates. Small boats only to Gamla Uppsala.

optics.colour: Clay-grey brown river; brown humic bay.
optics.turbidityCause: Uppland clay and humics.

hazards.name: Shallow river
hazards.danger: Too shallow for laden ships; boats or a walk (estimate).

phenomena: Clay-turbid spring flood over meadows
Ice every winter
Reed-lined bay shore
records.change_800_to_1066: Uplift moves the bay head south by perhaps a kilometre over the period (guess).
records.then_vs_now: The bay reached much closer to Uppsala; the Fyris valley floor was wet meadow and water.

records.name: The Åland sea and Saltvik's bay

tide.phaseNote: No tide; level-driven currents between the islands.
tide.notes: Åland uplift roughly 5 mm/yr (knowledge), so c. 800 the sea stood about 5-6 m higher (estimate): the Kvarnbo-Saltvik area lay on a sea bay that is now land and lakes (estimate).

waves.notes: Inside the archipelago sheltered; the open Åland Sea to the west is deep (about 300 m, knowledge) with a full Baltic sea in storms.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Currents of up to 1 kn through sounds (estimate).
sea.notes: Archipelago ice every winter c. 800 (knowledge of the modern regime plus -0.8 C).

optics.colour: Dark green over red granite; clear.
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton, CDOM.

hazards.name: Skerries
hazards.danger: Countless rocks awash (knowledge).

phenomena: Red granite skerries and pines
Sea ice and ice roads
Glassy calms between islands
Spring ice break-up
records.change_800_to_1066: About 0.5 m of uplift; bays shoal into lakes (estimate).
records.then_vs_now: Sea about 5-6 m higher; many of today's lakes and fields were bays.

records.name: The Vistula lagoon and the Drużno bay to Truso

tide.phaseNote: No tide; level follows the Baltic set-up through the inlet, damped (estimate).
tide.notes: Truso stood on the Nogat delta branch close to a bay, the modern Drużno lake, where it entered the shallow brackish lagoon (verified). Drużno is part of the lagoon cut off by alluvium, mean depth 1.2 m, max 2.5 m today (verified). The lagoon's opening to the sea in the 9th c. lay elsewhere than the modern Baltiysk strait (knowledge: the medieval inlet near Balga/Lochstädt; not verified). Lagoon seiche about 10 h (estimate, Merian L 90 km, h 2.7 m).

waves.notes: The long NE-SW axis lets a short steep chop build in a lengthwise gale (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Net outflow of Vistula/Nogat and Pregolya water; wind-driven circulation (knowledge).
sea.notes: About 90 km long, 10-24 km wide, mean 2.7 m, max about 5 m, 838 km2, salinity about 3 (verified).

optics.colour: Green-brown silty lagoon water; brown at the Nogat mouth.
optics.turbidityCause: River silt, wind-resuspended mud, phytoplankton.

salinityPsu.note: About 3 (verified); the Teutonic Order called it Mare Recens, the fresh sea (verified, 1246); near Truso fresh (estimate).

hazards.name: Silting delta mouths
hazards.danger: From the second half of the 10th c. silting of the Nogat began to cut Truso off (verified).

hazards.name: Lagoon ice
hazards.danger: Every winter (estimate).

phenomena: Wide flat lagoon with the wooded spit's dunes on the horizon
Reed-filled delta channels
Lagoon chop that rises fast in a NE wind
Ice every winter
records.change_800_to_1066: Truso declines after about 850 (levels file); the Nogat silts from the later 10th c. (verified). Drużno is gradually cut off by delta growth (verified mechanism, dates estimate).
records.then_vs_now: No dikes or polders of the Żuławy (13th c. onward, knowledge); Drużno an open bay of the lagoon; inlet at a different place (knowledge); no 2022 canal.

records.name: The Vistula mouth and the Motława at Gdańsk

tide.phaseNote: No tide; Baltic set-up backs up the river (estimate).
tide.tidalLimit: Set-up backs up the lower Vistula a few tens of km (estimate).
tide.notes: The Gdańsk Vistula (later the Dead Vistula) was the main mouth until the 1840 ice-jam breakthrough (Śmiała Wisła) and the 1889-1895 Vistula Cut (verified). c. 980 the stronghold stood by the Motława near its junction with that branch (levels file).

river.name: Vistula (Wisła), Gdańsk branch
river.notes: Mean 1,080 m3/s at the mouth (verified). Ice-jam floods are the river's typical disaster (verified). c. 800 the Nogat was a lesser branch and more water went to Gdańsk (knowledge). Low, flood, width and speeds are estimates.

waves.notes: Gdańsk bay is sheltered from the west by the Hel peninsula (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: River plume turning east along the coast (knowledge).
sea.notes: Gdańsk bay.

optics.colour: Yellow-brown silty river; a muddy plume in the green bay.
optics.turbidityCause: Vistula silt (loess and sand catchment).

hazards.name: Shifting mouth bars
hazards.danger: Sand bars and ice jams (knowledge).

hazards.name: Ice jams
hazards.danger: Sudden rises and flooding (verified).

phenomena: Muddy plume into the green bay
Spring ice drift and jams
Sand islands with willow
Mist over the delta
records.change_800_to_1066: Gdańsk's stronghold from about 980 (levels file); delta branches shift (guess).
records.then_vs_now: No dikes, no cuts (1840 and 1895, verified), no port basins; delta marsh and branches.

records.name: The Curonian lagoon to Wiskiauten (Kaup)

tide.phaseNote: No tide; the only outlet is the Klaipėda strait in the north, with level-driven currents in and out (knowledge).
tide.notes: Kaup lies by the lagoon's south shore (Wiskiauten) near the base of the spit; a major pagan trading centre c. 800-1016 (verified). Lagoon seiche about 9 h (estimate, Merian L 98 km, h 3.8 m).

waves.notes: Shallow lagoon chop; a long N-S fetch (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Net outflow north through the strait; the Neman (mean 678 m3/s, verified) supplies about 90% of inflow (verified).
sea.notes: 1,619 km2, 98 km by 46 km, mean 3.8 m, max 5.8 m, a freshwater lagoon (verified). Neman floods can rise 11-fold to more than 6,800 m3/s; severe floods about every 12-15 years (verified).

optics.colour: Green-brown fresh lagoon; today summer blue-green algal blooms (verified 2000s), c. 800 fewer (estimate).
optics.turbidityCause: Phytoplankton, Neman silt.

salinityPsu.note: Fresh in the south (Kaup), brackish pulses in the north near the strait (knowledge).

hazards.name: Shoals off the spit
hazards.danger: Shallow sand (knowledge).

hazards.name: Lagoon ice
hazards.danger: Every winter (estimate).

phenomena: Wooded dunes of the spit on the western skyline
Lagoon chop
Ice every winter, fishermen on it
Mosquito-swarm summer evenings
records.change_800_to_1066: Kaup ends about 1016 (verified). Spit stable and wooded.
records.then_vs_now: The spit was forested; the great wandering dunes and buried villages come only after 16th-18th c. deforestation (verified). The Klaipėda strait was not dredged.

records.name: The Courland coast, Liepāja lagoon and the Ālande (Grobiņa, Apuolė)

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Grobiņa lies 11 km east of Liepāja, its stronghold guarded on three sides by the Ālande (verified), which drains into the Liepāja lagoon-lake (verified). The lake today is 37.15 km2, max 3 m, mean 2 m, a lagoon behind a sand bar several km wide; its natural outlet kept closing with sand, so a canal was dug in 1697-1703 (verified). c. 800 the outlet channel was natural and shifting (estimate). Apuolė stands inland on the Luoba, about 8 km east of Skuodas (verified), up the Bārta system that feeds the same lagoon (verified Bārta inflow).

river.name: Ālande and Bārta
river.notes: River numbers are estimates (Bārta catchment roughly 2,000 km2, knowledge). Small craft only beyond the lagoon.

waves.notes: The outer coast is an open surf beach (Hs mean about 0.9 m, 99% about 3.5 m, estimate as O5).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak outflow through the shifting outlet.
sea.notes: Lagoon values; the open coast outside has the central Baltic sea state.

optics.colour: Brown-green shallow lagoon; brown rivers.
optics.turbidityCause: Humics, mud, plankton.

hazards.name: Outlet bar
hazards.danger: Shallow sand outlet that closes in storms (verified mechanism).

hazards.name: Surf coast
hazards.danger: Breaker bars along a harbourless coast (knowledge).

phenomena: Surf beach outside, calm reedy lagoon inside
Ice every winter
Sand outlet reshaped by each storm
records.change_800_to_1066: Grobiņa's Scandinavian colony ends by the mid-9th c. (verified); Apuolė is besieged by the Swedes in 854 (verified).
records.then_vs_now: No canal and no port of Liepāja; the outlet natural.

records.name: The Gulf of Riga

tide.phaseNote: No tide; Irbe strait currents are wind- and level-driven (knowledge).
tide.notes: Gulf seiche and set-up raise Riga's level by 1-2 m in westerly storms (knowledge). Until the 1567 spring flood the Daugava entered the sea at Vecāķi, east of today's mouth (verified).

waves.notes: Semi-enclosed basin; estimates.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak cyclonic circulation (knowledge).
sea.notes: 18,000 km2, mean 26 m, max 54 m (verified, a 66 m figure also given); thickest ice 90 cm in 1941-42; ice melts March-April (verified). With 793's climate the gulf ices most winters (estimate).

optics.colour: Olive-green, browner toward the Daugava mouth.
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton and river humics.

salinityPsu.note: Source says 6-10 (verified) which looks high for the surface; 5-6 surface is the usual value (knowledge); doubt noted.

hazards.name: Irbe strait shoals
hazards.danger: Shoals and sandbanks with ice in spring (knowledge).

hazards.name: Sea ice
hazards.danger: Ice floes until March-April; people trapped on floes (verified 2013).

phenomena: Ice floes in spring
Long sandy beaches with dunes
Brown Daugava plume
Westerly set-up flooding the river mouth
records.change_800_to_1066: Little; northern shores rise slowly.
records.then_vs_now: Daugava mouth at Vecāķi (verified); no Riga (1201), no moles.

records.name: The lower Daugava to Daugmale

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.tidalLimit: Gulf set-up backs up only the lowest 10-20 km (estimate); Daugmale, about 30 km up, is a free-flowing river c. 800.
tide.notes: Today Daugmale sits on the Riga HPP reservoir (1974, verified date); c. 800 the river below the rapids was lower and faster (estimate).

river.name: Daugava (Western Dvina)
river.notes: Mean 678 m3/s, runoff 21 km3/yr (verified); total fall 221 m, 99 m in Latvia (verified); about 150 rapids along the river, one of the rockiest rivers of eastern Europe (verified); width about 700 m at Riga and 1.5 km near the mouth, depth 8-9 m at Riga (verified); frequent spring ice jams (verified); the winter of 1708-09 had 1.7 m ice (verified). Flood flow, low flow, speeds and the width at Daugmale are estimates.

optics.colour: Brown humic river, coffee-coloured in the spring flood.
optics.turbidityCause: Humics from forest and bog, flood silt.

hazards.name: Ice jams
hazards.danger: Sudden floods behind jams (verified).

hazards.name: Rapids above Daugmale
hazards.danger: Boats towed, poled or portaged (estimate).

phenomena: Spring ice drift with jams and grinding floes
Brown flood water spreading over meadows
Fast smooth water above the first rapids
Dolomite cliffs on the banks
records.change_800_to_1066: Daugmale becomes the main market from about 900 (levels file).
records.then_vs_now: Three dams (Ķegums 1939, Pļaviņas 1965-68, Riga 1974, verified) have drowned the rapids and cliffs; c. 800 a free, fast, rocky river with spring floods and ice jams.

records.name: The Gulf of Finland

tide.phaseNote: A few centimetres of tide; level is wind set-up and the Baltic seiche, which pile up at the eastern end.
tide.notes: Frequent strong westerlies raise waves and surges that flood the Neva mouth (verified). The worst floods at the Neva mouth: 4.21 m on 7 Nov 1824, 3.69 m in 1924, 3.21 m in 1777 (verified); a 7.6 m figure for 1691 is given by the same page (verified but doubtful, pre-instrumental). So surges of 2-4 m at the head of the gulf are the extreme case; 1-1.5 m happen most autumns (estimate). Relative sea level c. 800: about 1-3 m higher on the Finnish and north Estonian coasts (estimate from uplift of 2-4 mm/yr, knowledge), near today at the Neva.

waves.notes: Record Hs 5.2 m with a single wave of about 9 m (15 Nov 2001) and Hs 5.2 m again in 2012 (verified, FMI). Mean and 99th percentile are estimates. The narrow gulf channels westerly seas along its axis.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak cyclonic circulation: inflow along the Estonian south coast, outflow along Finland (knowledge), 0.1-0.3 kn.
sea.notes: About 30,000 km2, 400 km long, 70-130 km wide, mean 38 m, max 115-123 m (verified; two figures given). Freezes every winter, late Nov to late Apr, from the east; usually fully frozen by late January (verified). Winter water near 0 C, summer surface 15-17 C (verified). For 793 add one to three weeks to the ice season (estimate from -0.8 C).

optics.colour: Olive green-brown; browner toward the east and the Neva plume.
optics.turbidityCause: High CDOM from the Neva and Finnish rivers; plankton.

salinityPsu.note: Falls from about 5-6 in the west to near 0 at the Neva mouth (knowledge). The en.wikipedia figure of 0.2-0.3 per mille at the surface is almost certainly a unit slip (per cent); doubt noted.

hazards.name: Skerries of the Finnish and Estonian coasts
hazards.danger: Granite skerries (north) and limestone klint shoals (south) (knowledge).

hazards.name: Sea ice
hazards.danger: Closes the gulf every winter; floes in spring (verified).

hazards.name: Westerly surge at the Neva mouth
hazards.danger: Water up 2-4 m in an autumn westerly (verified extremes).

phenomena: Sea ice and pressure ridges in winter
Ice break-up in April-May with floes and leads
Short steep westerly sea
White nights in June
Glassy calms and fog in spring
records.change_800_to_1066: Coastal uplift continues; MCA milder winters after 950. Otherwise the same.
records.then_vs_now: No St Petersburg, no flood barrier (2011), no dredged channels; north coasts 1-3 m lower land relative to sea.

sources.title: FMI, Wave height records in the Baltic Sea

records.name: The Narva river and its falls

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.tidalLimit: Gulf set-up reaches up to the falls, about 13 km from the sea (estimate).
tide.notes: The Narva falls (two arms either side of Kreenholm island, 60 m and 110 m wide, both 6.5 m high, verified) stop every boat: portage round them. Above the falls the river runs with rapids to Lake Peipus (knowledge).

river.name: Narva
river.notes: 77 km, mean 400 m3/s (verified). Low and flood flows, width and speeds are estimates; the lake damps the floods. Total fall about 30 m from Peipus (30 m asl, knowledge) to the sea.

optics.colour: Brown-green lake water, white foam at the falls.
optics.turbidityCause: Peipus plankton and humics.

hazards.name: Narva falls
hazards.danger: Impassable 6.5 m falls, 'at times the most powerful in Europe' (verified).

phenomena: Roaring falls with spray and foam lines below
Ice-free water below the falls in winter while the river freezes elsewhere (estimate)
Standing waves in the rapids
records.change_800_to_1066: None.
records.then_vs_now: The 1955 dam and reservoir have left the falls usually near dry (verified); c. 800 the full river ran over them.

records.name: Lake Peipus, the Warm lake narrows and Lake Pskov

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Wind set-up along the long axis tilts the lake by decimetres; seiche about 6 h for Peipus proper (estimate, Merian L 90 km, h 7.1 m). Seasonal level range about 1-1.5 m (knowledge).

waves.notes: A shallow lake with long fetch: short steep seas up to about 2 m in an autumn gale (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak flow from Lake Pskov north through the narrows (Lämmijärv) to the Narva outlet.
sea.notes: 3,555 km2, mean 7.1 m, max 15.3 m; Peipus proper 73%, Pskov 20%, Warm lake 7% (verified). Freezes late Nov-early Dec, thaws late Apr-early May (verified). The Battle on the Ice was fought on it on 5 April 1242 (verified), which shows how late the ice held in a cold year.

optics.colour: Grey-green to brownish, low transparency.
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton and river sediment (verified, transparency about 2.5 m).

hazards.name: Shoals and sand reefs
hazards.danger: Shallow sandy margins (knowledge).

hazards.name: Lake ice
hazards.danger: Thin ice early and late season (verified dates).

phenomena: Huge flat horizon with no shore visible
Steep short gale seas
Fishermen's ice in winter
Ice heaped on shore at break-up
Mayfly hatches and gnat clouds in summer
records.change_800_to_1066: None of note; Pleskov a town from 900 (levels file).
records.then_vs_now: Less eutrophic; transparency perhaps 3-4 m (guess) against about 2.5 m today (verified).

records.name: The Emajõgi to Tarbatu (Tartu)

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Tartu stands on the Emajõgi about 40 km above Lake Peipus (estimate). Peipus high water backs up the lower river (knowledge).

river.name: Emajõgi
river.notes: 100 km long today, 117 km in 1927 before the upper course was straightened; mean 70 m3/s; Estonia's only fully navigable river; the valley narrows to about 800 m at Tartu (verified). Width, speeds and flows other than the mean are estimates.

optics.colour: Dark brown 'mother river' water (the name means mother river).
optics.turbidityCause: Bog humics.

hazards.name: Spring flood over meadows
hazards.danger: Channel lost in flooded meadows (estimate).

phenomena: Dark slow water mirroring willows
Spring flood meadows kilometres wide
Ice every winter
records.change_800_to_1066: Tarbatu fort; Yaroslav the Wise founds Yuryev here in 1030 (knowledge).
records.then_vs_now: The upper course still meandered (straightened in the 1930s, verified).

records.name: The Velikaya at Pleskov (Pskov)

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: The Krom stands where the Pskova enters the Velikaya, about 10 km above Lake Pskov (estimate).

river.name: Velikaya
river.notes: 430 km, mean 134 m3/s, over 200 m wide in Pskov and 320 m at the Alexander Nevsky bridge, spring flood up to 1.5 m, ice Nov-Apr, a rapid reach that floods hide (verified). Other numbers are estimates.

optics.colour: Brown-green.
optics.turbidityCause: Humics, flood silt.

hazards.name: Upstream rapids
hazards.danger: Shallow rocky reach at low water (verified existence).

phenomena: Wide calm river under limestone walls
Ice drift in April
records.change_800_to_1066: Pleskov a town from 900 (levels file).
records.then_vs_now: No embankments or bridges.

records.name: The Neva

tide.phaseNote: No real tide; westerly surges of the gulf run up the river (verified floods at the mouth).
tide.tidalLimit: Surge set-up felt for perhaps 20-30 km up the river (estimate).
tide.notes: The way from the gulf to Lake Ladoga, 74 km (verified), upstream against the current: sail with a westerly, tow or row otherwise.

river.name: Neva
features: Ivanovskiye rapids (210 m wide, 4-4.5 m deep)
river.notes: 74 km, 400-600 m wide (1,000-1,250 m in the delta), 8-11 m deep (24 m max), mean discharge given as 2,628 m3/s (other sources about 2,500, knowledge), max 4,550 m3/s; Ivanovskiye rapids 210 m wide, 4.0-4.5 m deep, flow 0.8-1.1 m/s (verified, though rapid-core currents of 3-4 m/s are reported in other literature, knowledge; doubt noted). Ice early Dec to early Apr, 0.3-0.6 m thick (verified). Lake-fed, so very steady: highest flow in early summer after Ladoga fills (knowledge). Fall about 5 m over 74 km (verified lake level 5 m asl).

optics.colour: Clear dark grey-green lake water (Ladoga outflow), not muddy.
optics.turbidityCause: Ladoga water: low silt, moderate humics.

hazards.name: Ivanovskiye rapids
hazards.danger: Narrowing with fast water and boulders; towing upstream (verified dimensions).

hazards.name: Westerly surge
hazards.danger: Delta islands flooded by 2-4 m surges (verified extremes).

phenomena: Powerful, smooth, fast clear river
Boils and swirls over the rapids
Ice drift twice: river ice in April, Ladoga ice in May (knowledge)
White nights
records.change_800_to_1066: None.
records.then_vs_now: A wild delta of marsh and forest islands; no city, embankments, bridges or dredging.

records.name: Lake Ladoga

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Wind set-up: annual swings of 50-70 cm, up to 3 m at most (verified); the page also gives seiches 'up to 3-4 m', which is probably set-up plus seiche at the shallow south shore, not a free seiche (doubt noted). Merian period of the fundamental seiche about 5.7 h (estimate, L 219 km, h 47 m).

waves.swellFrom: N (long fetch onto the shallow south shore)
waves.notes: Maximum recorded wave about 6 m; in severe storms the water is almost all foam (verified). The south shore shallows make breaking seas (knowledge). Mean and 99th percentile are estimates.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak cyclonic circulation (knowledge).
sea.notes: 17,891 km2, mean 47.3 m, max 230-260 m, surface 5 m asl; inflows Svir 790, Volkhov 580, Vuoksi 540 m3/s (verified). Coastal ice from December, the centre only in very severe winters, break-up April-May (verified). For 793 the centre freezes more often (estimate: 1 in 3).

optics.colour: Cold steel grey-green offshore; brown off the Volkhov and Svir mouths.
optics.turbidityCause: Humics from the rivers; low plankton.

hazards.name: Southern shoals and reefs
hazards.danger: Shallows, stony reefs and banks (verified).

hazards.name: Autumn gales
hazards.danger: Seas to 6 m (verified); the reason Peter the Great dug the Ladoga canal (knowledge).

hazards.name: Northern skerries
hazards.danger: Fjords and skerries (verified).

phenomena: Freshwater sea with no far shore
Foam-white storm seas
Very clear water off Valaam (Secchi 8-9 m summer, over 10 m winter, verified)
River-mouth brown plumes (0.3-0.9 m Secchi, verified)
Ice shove and ice piles on the south shore in spring
Warm south shallows (+24 C in August) against a cold centre (verified)
records.change_800_to_1066: None.
records.then_vs_now: No canals along the south shore (18th-19th c.), no Volkhov dam; same lake.

records.name: The lower Volkhov: Aldeigjuborg and the Volkhov rapids

tide.phaseNote: No tide; Ladoga's level backs up the lowest reach.
tide.notes: Staraya Ladoga is 'the only possible harbor for sea vessels that could not navigate through the Volkhov' (verified): sea ships stopped here, below the rapids, and goods went on in river boats. Founded 753 (dendro, verified); coins from 786/787 (verified).

river.name: Volkhov
features: the Volkhov (Gostinopolye) rapids above Ladoga, about 10 km long
river.notes: 224 km; mean 580-593, min 44, max 2,900 m3/s; ice late Nov to early April (verified). The rapids made passage very hard, especially at low water, and the 1926 dam about 25 km above the mouth flooded them (verified). Rapid length and fall (about 10 km and 10-11 m, roughly the dam's head) are estimates (knowledge, not verified); with pilots and towing, upstream passage at low water meant unloading (knowledge). Mean gradient over the whole river about 0.06 m/km (Ilmen 18 m asl to Ladoga 5 m, estimate); concentrated in the rapids.

optics.colour: Yellow-brown Ilmen water (verified yellowish), white water on the rapids.
optics.turbidityCause: Organic matter and silt from Ilmen.

hazards.name: Volkhov rapids
hazards.where: Above Staraya Ladoga, up to the present dam site
hazards.danger: Fast broken water over limestone ledges; pilots, towing, unloading at low water (estimate).

hazards.name: Spring ice drift
hazards.danger: Ice floes grinding past the harbour (estimate).

phenomena: Standing waves and white water on the rapids
High limestone banks with the Ladoga hillfort
Brown flood water in May
Ice break-up drift
records.change_800_to_1066: Ladoga a hub throughout; a stone fortress from the late 9th c. (knowledge).
records.then_vs_now: The 1926 Volkhov dam drowned the rapids (verified): today a slow reservoir reach where in 800 there was white water.

records.name: The upper Volkhov at Hólmgarðr (Novgorod)

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Novgorod and Rurikovo Gorodishche sit just below the Volkhov's outflow from Lake Ilmen (levels file). The upper Volkhov can stop or reverse: the chronicle records it flowing backward for 5 days in 1176, and its flow stopped in April 2013 (verified): when the Msta and other tributaries flood while Ilmen is low, water runs back into the lake (verified mechanism).

river.name: Volkhov (upper)
river.notes: Discharge as at the mouth (verified); here it equals the Ilmen outflow plus local inflow. Flood rise follows Ilmen's 7.4 m range (verified for the lake), damped (estimate 4-6 m). Width and speeds are estimates.

optics.colour: Yellowish-brown (verified for Ilmen water).
optics.turbidityCause: Organic matter.

hazards.name: Spring flood
hazards.danger: Meadows and lower town flooded by several metres (estimate).

phenomena: Flow reversal: debris drifting toward the lake
Wide spring floods around the Gorodishche
Ice Nov-Apr (verified)
records.change_800_to_1066: Hólmgarðr grows from the Gorodishche (9th c.) to the town of Novgorod (10th c.) (levels file; knowledge).
records.then_vs_now: No embankments; the Ilmen outflow natural (no Volkhov dam backwater).

records.name: Lake Ilmen

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Level swings up to 7.4 m a year, lowest in March, highest in May (verified); area 733-2,090 km2, mean 982 km2 (verified). So in spring the lake more than doubles and drowns the Lovat-Msta delta; in late summer the shores are wide mud and sand flats (estimate). Seiche about 4 h (estimate, Merian L 45 km, h 3.5 m).

waves.notes: Shallow: a short, steep, muddy sea builds fast in a gale (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Through-flow from the Lovat, Msta and Shelon to the Volkhov.
sea.notes: Max 10 m, mean 3-4 m, ice Nov-Apr, July water 19-20 C (verified).

optics.colour: Yellowish from organic matter (verified); muddy in wind.
optics.turbidityCause: Organic matter and wind-stirred mud.

hazards.name: Short steep gale sea
hazards.danger: Swamping risk for laden river boats (estimate).

hazards.name: Delta shoals at low water
hazards.danger: Channels hard to find in late summer (estimate).

phenomena: Spring flood lake spreading over meadows and forests
Muddy wind-sea
Ice Nov-Apr
Late-summer mud flats with birds
records.change_800_to_1066: None.
records.then_vs_now: Unregulated; same natural range.

records.name: The Lovat (to the portages)

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Upstream from Ilmen, then portages to the Daugava/Dnieper headwaters (the levels file's haul).

river.name: Lovat
features: rapids and small falls in the middle course near the Loknya confluence and below Kholm
river.notes: 530 km, falls from about 170 to 18.1 m asl (verified, about 0.29 m/km average); 10-15 m wide upstream, 50-60 m at Kholm, over 100 m below the Kunya, up to 340 m in the Ilmen lowland (verified); mean 170 m3/s at the mouth; 55% of the year's water passes from late March through May (verified); 'many rapids and waterfalls' in the middle course (verified). Low and flood flows, depth and flood rise are estimates.

optics.colour: Brown humic river.
optics.turbidityCause: Bog humics, spring silt.

hazards.name: Middle-course rapids
hazards.danger: Shallow rocky rapids at summer low water; towing and unloading (verified existence).

phenomena: Narrow winding forest river
Spring flood through the forest
Shallow riffles and sandbars in summer
records.change_800_to_1066: None.
records.then_vs_now: Unregulated then and largely now; timber rafting has scarred the banks since (verified ended 1990s).

records.name: The middle Daugava at Polotesk (Polotsk)

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Upstream from Daugmale through the Latvian rapids, then a long forest river to Polotsk at the Polota mouth, then the haul to the Lovat or Dnieper (levels file).

river.name: Daugava (Western Dvina)
river.notes: Width about 200 m in the middle reach (verified as the width 'between the highland areas'); rapids over Devonian dolomite above Vitebsk for 12 km and frequent spring ice jams (verified); about 150 rapids in all (verified). Discharge at Polotsk (about 250 m3/s mean, knowledge, not verified), flood rise and speeds are estimates.

optics.colour: Brown humic river.
optics.turbidityCause: Humics, flood silt.

hazards.name: Rapids
hazards.where: Many reaches, worst in Latvia and above Vitebsk
hazards.danger: Shallow rocky riffles; towing and portage at low water (verified existence).

hazards.name: Ice jams
hazards.danger: Sudden rises (verified).

phenomena: Riffles and boulder rapids with standing waves
High forested banks
Spring ice drift
Morning mist in the valley
records.change_800_to_1066: Polotesk appears from 862 (levels file) and is a principality by 980.
records.then_vs_now: Five hydro dams now (verified) drown many rapids; c. 800 the whole river ran free.

records.name: The upper Dnieper at Gnezdovo and Smolensk

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: The first Dnieper reach after the portages from the Lovat/Daugava side; downstream from here all the way to the rapids (levels file).

river.name: Dnieper (upper)
features: sand bars and riffles at low water
Gnezdovo's harbour by the Svinets stream mouth
river.notes: Upper-course speeds 0.3-1.2 m/s (verified, ru.wikipedia, upper Dnieper); the river is navigable up to Dorogobuzh above Smolensk (verified). Width 'up to 30 m' in the source is the uppermost course (verified); at Smolensk about 100-150 m (knowledge). Discharge at Smolensk (about 110 m3/s), flood rise and low flow are estimates (knowledge, not verified).

optics.colour: Brown-green river over yellow sand bars.
optics.turbidityCause: Humics, flood silt.

hazards.name: Shoals and riffles
hazards.danger: Boats ground; tow or lighten (estimate).

phenomena: Yellow sand bars and willows
Spring flood over the meadows
Ice drift in April
Summer evening mist on the river
records.change_800_to_1066: Gnezdovo flourishes from about 880 and gives way to Smolensk about 1020 (levels file).
records.then_vs_now: Unregulated then and largely now in this reach; more forest, more beaver dams on the side streams (knowledge).

records.name: The middle Dnieper: Lyubech, Vyshgorod, Kiev, Vitichev

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: At Kiev the boats gathered in the Podil harbour on the Pochaina (levels file), a side channel of the Dnieper (knowledge). Vitichev below Kiev was the assembly point for the convoy south (knowledge, Constantine VII).

river.name: Dnieper (middle)
features: high right bank (Kiev hills), low left floodplain
river.notes: At Kiev: mean 1,370 m3/s, spring flood about 7,000 m3/s; width 200-1,200 m and depth to 8 m in the middle course; 55-57% of the year's water passes in March-May; gradient 0.09 m/km; ice at Kiev about 17 Dec to 24 Mar (verified, ru.wikipedia, modern normals). For 793 add one to two weeks of ice (estimate). Flood rise, low flow and speeds are estimates (the 1931 flood peak of about 23,000 m3/s is knowledge, not verified).

optics.colour: Green-brown, tawny in flood; white sand beaches.
optics.turbidityCause: Silt and humics (Pripyat and Desna bring bog water).

hazards.name: Shifting sand bars
hazards.danger: Channel moves yearly (knowledge).

hazards.name: Spring flood
hazards.danger: Floodplain drowned kilometres wide in April-May (estimate).

phenomena: Broad river with islands under high loess bluffs
Spring flood lake across the left-bank meadows
Summer heat haze and sandbars
Ice drift in March
records.change_800_to_1066: Kiev becomes the Rus' capital from 882 (levels file); the right bank's bluffs erode; channels shift.
records.then_vs_now: The Kiev (1960-64) and Kaniv (1963-75) reservoirs (verified) now drown this reach into lakes; c. 800 a free braided river with a seasonal flood.

records.name: The Desna at Chernigov

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: A side trip up the Desna from its confluence just above Kiev (levels file).

river.name: Desna
river.notes: 1,130 km, mean 360 m3/s at the mouth, ice December to early April, a large spring flood (verified). Values at Chernigov (slightly less than at the mouth), width, flood rise and speeds are estimates.

optics.colour: Clearer brown-green over pale sand.
optics.turbidityCause: Humics; little silt (sandy catchment).

hazards.name: Sand bars at low water
hazards.danger: Groundings in late summer (estimate).

phenomena: Tight meanders with white sand beaches
Oxbow lakes with lilies
Spring flood meadows
records.change_800_to_1066: Chernigov a town from 900 (levels file).
records.then_vs_now: Unregulated then and now; more forest.

records.name: The Dnieper rapids (the Porogi)

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: 66 km of rapids with a total drop of 50 m: nine major rapids, about 30-40 lesser ones and about 60 islands (verified). The largest, Nenasytets ('insatiable'), was 2.4 km long and over 1 km wide, its roar heard kilometres away (verified). Travellers carried their boats round seven rapids while guarding against Pecheneg attack (verified); Constantine VII gives Norse and Slavic names, e.g. Essoupi 'Don't sleep', and the Slavic 'island rapid' (verified). Below them the Kichkas crossing and Khortytsia island (knowledge).

river.name: Dnieper (rapids reach)
features: portage paths on the right bank
river.notes: Gradient 50 m / 66 km = 0.76 m/km average (computed from verified figures), concentrated in the ledges. Discharge (about 1,600 m3/s, between Kiev's 1,370 and the mouth's 1,670, verified endpoints), speeds and flood rise are estimates. The convoy went down in June after the flood (Constantine VII, knowledge), when water still covered many ledges.

optics.colour: Green-brown river broken into white water over black granite.
optics.turbidityCause: Silt; aeration foam in the rapids.

hazards.name: Nenasytets (Aifor)
hazards.danger: Impassable: full portage (verified size; portage, knowledge of Constantine VII).

hazards.name: Lesser rapids and ledges
hazards.danger: Boats lined, poled or dragged along the edges, crews wading (knowledge).

hazards.name: Pecheneg ambush
hazards.where: Portage paths and the Kichkas crossing
hazards.danger: Not water but the reason the rapids were deadly; Sviatoslav killed here in 972 (knowledge).

phenomena: Roaring white water audible from far off (verified)
Standing waves and holes below granite ledges
Spray rainbows in sun
Eddies and whirlpools below the rapids
Pelicans and cormorants on the rocks (knowledge)
records.change_800_to_1066: None in the water; the Pechenegs arrive in the steppe in the late 9th c. (knowledge) and make the portage a battle.
records.then_vs_now: Drowned since 1932 by the Dnieper dam's reservoir (verified); Zaporizhzhia means 'beyond the rapids' (verified). After the 2023 Kakhovka dam destruction the lower river changed but the rapids reach remains drowned upstream of the Dnipro dam (knowledge).

records.name: The lower Dnieper and its liman, out to Berezan

tide.phaseNote: Black Sea tide is a few cm; wind set-up moves the liman level (knowledge).
tide.tidalLimit: Set-up backs up to about Kherson (estimate).
tide.notes: From the rapids to the liman the river slows (0.6-0.7 m/s lower reach, verified) through a wide delta (about 350 km2, verified) into the brackish Dnieper-Bug liman; Berezan island sits off the liman mouth (Black Sea region, O19). Black Sea level c. 800 was near today's, perhaps slightly lower (knowledge, not verified).

river.name: Dnieper (lower)
features: the Great Meadow (Velykyi Luh) floodplain forest below Khortytsia
river.notes: Mean 1,670 m3/s at Kherson (verified); ice at Zaporizhzhia about 5 Jan-9 Mar and at Kherson about 3 Jan-3 Mar in modern normals (verified); in mild winters only partial ice (estimate). Width, flood and gradient are estimates.

waves.swellFrom: SW from the open sea at the mouth
waves.notes: Liman chop (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: River outflow along the north side (estimate).
sea.notes: Liman values are estimates.

optics.colour: Green-brown river; olive-green liman; blue-green Black Sea beyond.
optics.turbidityCause: Silt and plankton.

salinityPsu.note: Fresh in the delta, increasing westward through the liman to brackish (verified direction); about 10-15 at the mouth (estimate).

hazards.name: Delta shoals
hazards.danger: Shallow channels and the Kinburn spit bar (knowledge).

phenomena: Huge reed delta with pelicans
Warm shallow liman
Summer thunderstorm squalls over the steppe
records.change_800_to_1066: None of note.
records.then_vs_now: The Kakhovka reservoir (1950-56, destroyed June 2023, verified) drowned the Great Meadow floodplain forest; c. 800 that was a vast forested floodplain with channels.

records.name: The Svir

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: From Ladoga up the Svir to Lake Onega: 224 km against the current (verified length).

river.name: Svir
features: rapids in the middle course (drowned by the dams)
spring ice jams in the lower course
river.notes: 224 km, mean 790 m3/s, 100 m wide in narrow places, speed 0.5-10.6 km/h (0.14-2.9 m/s), rapids in the middle course flooded by the dams, spring floods in the lower course made worse by ice jams (verified); the Upper Svir dam was completed 1952 (verified); the Lower Svir dam about 1933 (knowledge). Fall about 28 m from Onega (about 33 m asl, knowledge) to Ladoga (5 m, verified). Other values estimates; the 10-12 km Ivinsky widening in the source is the reservoir, not the natural river.

optics.colour: Dark tea-brown lake-outflow water.
optics.turbidityCause: Onega humics.

hazards.name: Svir rapids
hazards.danger: Fast water to about 3 m/s over rock (verified speed range); towing upstream (estimate).

phenomena: Fast dark water through pine and spruce forest
Boils over the rapids
Ice jams in spring
records.change_800_to_1066: None.
records.then_vs_now: Two dams (1930s, 1952) drowned the rapids (verified); c. 800 a fast wild river.

records.name: Lake Onega (to the Vytegra and the haul to the Kovzha)

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: The Volga road crosses the south of the lake to the Vytegra, then a haul to the Kovzha and down to Lake Beloye (route assumption: the later Mariinsk way; the levels file says the way by Beloozero is to check). Fundamental seiche about 8 h (estimate, Merian L 245 km, h 30 m).

waves.notes: Waves of 2-3 m are not uncommon and may reach 5 m (verified). Mean and 99th percentile are estimates.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Weak; outflow to the Svir (17.6 km3/yr, verified).
sea.notes: 9,891 km2, about 245 by 90 km, mean 30 m, max 127 m; freezes near the coast in late Nov-Dec and in the centre around mid-January; thaw reaches the lake in May; open-lake surface 20-24 C in summer, deep water 2-6 C (verified).

optics.colour: Clear dark brown-green in the deep parts; brown in the bays.
optics.turbidityCause: Humics; visibility 7-8 m in the deep parts, about 1 m in bays (verified).

hazards.name: Gale seas
hazards.danger: 2-3 m common, to 5 m (verified).

hazards.name: Rocky shores and skerries
hazards.danger: Granite skerries (knowledge).

phenomena: Dark clear water over granite
Freshwater storm seas
Ice from Dec to May
White nights in June
records.change_800_to_1066: None.
records.then_vs_now: No canals or the Volga-Baltic waterway (19th-20th c., verified succession); same lake.

records.name: Lake Beloye and the Sheksna source at Beloozero

tide.phaseNote: No tide.
tide.notes: Beloozero stood at the Sheksna's source (verified: the ancient city at the river's source, known from 862, with excavations at the 'Old City' 2.5 km from the source). Seiche about 4 h (estimate, Merian L 46 km, h 4 m).

waves.notes: Round lake of about 46 km diameter (verified): every wind has full fetch over shallow water, so steep muddy seas build quickly (estimate).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Outflow to the Sheksna.
sea.notes: 1,130 km2, at 113 m asl (verified). Max depth given as 34 m by en.wikipedia (verified) but about 20 m in other sources (knowledge), and the lake is mostly shallow (mean about 4-5 m, knowledge); doubt noted. Ice roughly Nov to early May (estimate, as the Sheksna's late Oct-Dec to Apr-May, verified).

optics.colour: Whitish-grey turbid water in wind (the lake's name, 'white', is often explained this way, knowledge), brown when calm.
optics.turbidityCause: Wind-stirred clay and silt on a shallow bottom.

hazards.name: Short steep lake sea
hazards.danger: Dangerous to small laden boats; the Belozersk bypass canal was dug in the 19th c. for this reason (knowledge).

phenomena: Milky grey wind-stirred water
Wide flat horizon with forest rim
Ice Nov-May
records.change_800_to_1066: Beloozero a town from about 950 (levels file); the town later moved to today's Belozersk (verified history of moves, dates knowledge).
