tide.notes: The Rhone's rhythm is seasonal: snowmelt high water in late spring, violent rain floods in autumn and winter.

river.name: Rhone (Rhodanus)
features: a bridge of boats at Arles (knowledge)
river.notes: Mean 1,690 m3/s at Beaucaire 1920-2011 (fr.wikipedia, Rhone); 1,710 (en.wikipedia). The Rhone divides at Arles into the Grand Rhone and the Petit Rhone (en.wikipedia); the Petit Rhone leaves at Fourques and runs about 57 km to Saintes-Maries (fr.wikipedia); today the Grand Rhone carries about ten times the Petit Rhone's flow and averages 500 m wide (fr.wikipedia Grand-Rhone). Low flow, flood peak, current, depth and gradient are estimates; record floods in the 19th century and 2003 were of the order of 11,000-13,000 m3/s at Beaucaire (knowledge, verify on Banque Hydro). Ice: the Rhone froze over in the hardest winters (the chronicle's 821/822 lists the Rhine, Danube, Elbe and Seine, not the Rhone); one in about 30 winters with shore ice and floes at Arles under the 793 cooling (guess).

optics.colour: Opaque grey-green (glacial silt) in summer snowmelt, milky jade at low water, brown-grey in rain floods
optics.turbidityCause: Glacial and Alpine silt (summer), Durance and Cevenol rain sediment (autumn)

Milky glacial-green summer water
Floating trees in autumn floods
Ferries and the bridge of boats at Arles
Mosquito clouds and evening mist over the Camargue
records.change_800_to_1066: The delta's arms shifted through the Middle Ages and were only later embanked (fr.wikipedia, Delta du Rhone); dykes begin in the Middle Ages (fr.wikipedia, Camargue). c. 800 the main sea mouths were not today's: the eastern Rhone of Saint-Ferreol and the central Rhone d'Ulmet carried much of the flow, with the Grand Rhone's present lower course and mouths formed from the 15th century and the Bras de Fer abandoned for the Canal des Launes in 1711 (knowledge, from the delta studies of Arnaud-Fassetta and Provansal; not verified this session, guess for the exact split). The delta coast c. 800 lay several km inland of today's Grand Rhone mouth (guess). Arles is a Carolingian city with a river port; sacked by Saracens in 842 and 869 (knowledge).
records.then_vs_now: No dams (the Swiss and French Rhone barrages), no CNR canal, no embankments: higher sediment load, a wilder seasonal swing, wider and shallower in places (estimate). No modern Grand Rhone channel to the sea.

records.name: The Strait of Messina (Scylla and Charybdis)
levels: O16 to O17 and O18 join

tide.phaseNote: The Tyrrhenian and Ionian tides are nearly in opposition, so the level difference across the strait (up to 27 cm, an average slope of 1.7 cm per km) drives the current back and forth every 6 hours: the 'montante' runs north, the 'scendente' south (it.wikipedia, Stretto di Messina).
tide.notes: Tidal current up to 300 cm/s (5.8 knots); wind-driven drift to 80 cm/s; a permanent density current of 30 cm/s; theoretical maximum 560 cm/s; more than 200 cm/s in the Ganzirri-Punta Pezzo section in both directions; over 750,000 m3/s pass at 200 cm/s (it.wikipedia, citing Tomasino 1995 and Vercelli 1922-23).

waves.notes: Estimate. With wind against the current the strait raises steep standing seas.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Permanent density current 30 cm/s (it.wikipedia)
sea.notes: 3.1 km wide between Torre Faro and Villa San Giovanni, 5.1 km at Messina (en.wikipedia); the sill along Ganzirri-Punta Pezzo is 80-120 m deep (it.wikipedia). Where waters of different density meet, 'tagli' (discontinuity waves, 'scale di mare') form near Ganzirri, Torre Faro and Punta Pezzo; 'garofali', 'bastardi' and oily-calm patches are true whirlpools from opposing currents over the uneven bottom; Charybdis forms south of Capo Peloro on the northbound (montante) current, Scylla on the Calabrian side (it.wikipedia). The whirlpool is dangerous only to small craft in extreme conditions (en.wikipedia, Charybdis); a 9th-century ship of 15-20 m is small craft.

optics.colour: Intense dark blue with green-white lines where the 'tagli' meet; cold upwelled water

records.then_vs_now: The currents are physical and the same; the shoreline and Capo Peloro spit have changed with earthquakes (knowledge, estimate).

records.then_vs_now: Mahdia's rock-cut harbour is the period's; modern ports are later; the water is unchanged.

records.name: The Adriatic (open sea of O17)

tide.phaseNote: The semidiurnal tide turns about an amphidromic point east of Ancona, so the range is near zero mid-basin and grows to the head of the gulf; amplitudes usually stay below 30 cm (en.wikipedia, Adriatic). The diurnal part is strong, so the two daily tides are unequal (Venice and Trieste tables, Oct 2026).
tide.notes: The basin seiches lengthwise with a period of about 21.5 hours and an amplitude around 0.5 m at the ends (en.wikipedia, Acqua alta); sirocco set-up plus seiche plus spring tide is what floods Venice.

waves.swellFrom: SE (sirocco/jugo, the long fetch up the basin); the bora is offshore from the Croatian coast and raises a short, steep sea on the Italian side
waves.notes: A 150 km/h bora in Feb 2012 raised waves of 7 m (en.wikipedia, Bora). Mean and Hs99 estimates. Bora seas are short, high and white-crested (en.wikipedia, Bora).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Anticlockwise: north along the Croatian coast, south along the Italian coast (the Western Adriatic Current, carrying Po water, 0.2-0.5 m/s); 75% of the water entering at Otranto recirculates (en.wikipedia, Adriatic; speeds knowledge, estimate)
sea.notes: Mean depth about 252-260 m, maximum 1,233 m; the north rarely exceeds 100 m and is only 15 m at the NW end; the Middle Adriatic Pit 270 m; the South Adriatic Pit 1,200 m (en.wikipedia). Bora: cold dry gusts to 180 km/h (en.wikipedia, Adriatic), 220 km/h at Senj, record 248 km/h at the Maslenica bridge in 1998; peaks in winter; sustained up to 67-68 hours in Dalmatia; sea smoke; the sea froze at Senj (1956) and Makarska (1963) during bora (en.wikipedia, Bora). Sea ice may appear in shallow coastal areas (en.wikipedia, Adriatic). Sirocco (jugo): warm, humid, Saharan dust, long seas.

optics.colour: Clear blue in the south and along the Croatian islands; greenish and paler in the north and along the Italian coast where Po water spreads
optics.turbidityCause: Po and Alpine river input in the north-west (the Po alone 28% of the river discharge, 1,569 m3/s; total up to 5,700 m3/s, en.wikipedia); karst coast clear

salinityPsu.note: 38-39 in the open basin (en.wikipedia); fresher (30-36) in the north-west under the Po plume (estimate)

hazards.name: Velebit channel bora
hazards.danger: Bora gusts to 220 km/h, spray sheets, sea smoke (en.wikipedia, Bora)

hazards.name: Po delta shoals
hazards.danger: Shifting sandbanks off the mouths (estimate)

phenomena: Bora: a dark line racing across the sea, white spray blown flat, a cold blue sky, sea smoke in winter
Sirocco: grey, humid, long seas rolling north, a dull yellow sun
Acqua alta at the head of the gulf
Po plume: a green-brown tongue along the Italian coast
Glassy calms and haze in summer
records.change_800_to_1066: Venice rises from Byzantine dependency to a sea power; Comacchio is burned by Venice in 932 (levels_793.json to-date). The Po delta keeps growing about 4 m a year between 1000 BC and 1200 AD (en.wikipedia, Po); the big diversion at Ficarolo is 1152, after the game.
records.then_vs_now: No modern delta lobe of the Po (12 km of today's delta did not exist before 1152, en.wikipedia Po); coastline of the north-west further inland; no modern subsidence from gas extraction.

records.name: The Gulf of Venice: the sea off the lidos, from the Piave to the Po mouths

tide.phaseNote: Venice 0.79 m and Trieste 0.77 m daily ranges on 7 Oct 2026 approaching springs, 0.14 m at neap (tide tables); unequal highs show the diurnal part. Spring 1.0 m is an estimate.
tide.notes: The biggest tide in the Mediterranean outside Gabes and the Strait. Seiche of 21.5 h and up to 0.5 m adds (en.wikipedia, Acqua alta).

waves.swellFrom: SE (sirocco up the whole Adriatic) and ENE (bora across the gulf from Trieste)
waves.notes: Estimate. Very shallow (15 m at the NW end, en.wikipedia): storm waves break on the outer bars off the lidos.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Southward coastal current carrying river water along the lidos, 0.1-0.3 m/s (knowledge, estimate)
sea.notes: Winter water drops to 9 C on the north-western coast today (en.wikipedia, Adriatic), so about 8 C in 793 (decision 17). The sea froze inshore in the hardest winters (estimate from the bora freezes at Senj and Makarska, en.wikipedia Bora).

optics.colour: Green to olive-green, milky after storms, brown off the river mouths
optics.turbidityCause: Brenta, Piave, Adige and Po silt; resuspension in 10-20 m water; spring plankton blooms

salinityPsu.note: Freshened by the rivers; 30 or less near the mouths in flood (estimate)

hazards.name: Outer bars off the lidos
hazards.danger: Breaking in sirocco and bora (estimate)

hazards.name: Port mouths (bocche)
hazards.danger: Shallow, shifting, with ebb streams to 2-3 knots; c. 800 more numerous and shallower than today's three dredged mouths (estimate)

phenomena: Sea fog on calm winter days (caligo, knowledge)
Bora spray lines; snow on the Alps beyond
Sirocco surge pushing the sea over the lido dunes
Brown river plumes along the shore
records.change_800_to_1066: The coast and inlets shift with every flood; Metamauco (the old Malamocco on the lido) is the ducal seat 742-811 and is drowned by a storm surge in 1116 (en.wikipedia, Malamocco), after the game. The Po's main mouths are at the Volano and Primaro, south of today's delta (it.wikipedia, Rotta di Ficarolo).
records.then_vs_now: No murazzi sea walls (18th century), no jetties at the inlets (19th century), no MOSE barriers. Sea level some 1 m lower relative to the land than today (subsidence plus sea rise; Venice lost 23 cm since 1897 alone, en.wikipedia Acqua alta; the 800 figure is an estimate).

sources.title: Adriatic Sea (en): 15 m at the NW end, 9 C winter

records.name: The Venetian lagoon to Rivoaltus (Rialto)

tide.phaseNote: Lags the sea by about an hour inside the lagoon (estimate); range as the Gulf of Venice (Venice table 0.14-0.79 m in early Oct 2026, rising to springs).
tide.tidalLimit: The lagoon's landward edge and the lower reaches of the Brenta, Sile and Piave which then emptied into it (estimate)
tide.notes: Acqua alta: 'marea sostenuta' +80 to +109 cm, very high +110 to +139, exceptional +140 and above at Punta della Salute; record +194 cm on 4 Nov 1966, +187 cm on 12 Nov 2019 (it.wikipedia, Acqua alta); most frequent in autumn and spring; the causes are tide plus the 21.5 h seiche plus sirocco set-up, with the bora holding water in the lagoon (it.wikipedia). Documented floods before 1100 include 589, 782, 840 and 885 (en.wikipedia, Acqua alta). The streams in the inlets and main channels run 1-2.5 knots at springs (estimate).

waves.swellFrom: none inside; the sea swell stops at the inlets
waves.notes: Estimate: short steep chop in a bora over 10-15 km of 1-2 m water.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Tidal channels (canali) ebb and flood; river water flowing out through the inlets (estimate)
sea.notes: About 550 km2, mean depth 1.2 m, maximum 21.5 m; roughly 8% land, 11% open water and channels, 80% mud flats, shallows and salt marsh; three inlets today (Lido, Malamocco, Chioggia) (en.wikipedia, Venetian Lagoon). The Malamocco inlet is 380 m wide and 14 m deep today (en.wikipedia, Malamocco). c. 800 the Brenta, Bacchiglione, Sile and Piave still entered the lagoon (diverted in the 15th-17th centuries, en.wikipedia Venetian Lagoon; Brenta: a canal from Stra to the sea in the 16th century, en.wikipedia Brenta), so the lagoon was fresher, siltier and had more reed marsh; there were more and shallower inlets (estimate). The lagoon freezes over in the hardest winters (estimate; the Adriatic coast froze in 1956 and 1963 bora winters, en.wikipedia Bora).

optics.colour: Opaque green-jade in the shallows, grey-brown near the river mouths, darker green in the channels; mirror-flat in calm
optics.turbidityCause: Wind resuspension of mud on the flats; river silt (more c. 800 than today); plankton

salinityPsu.note: 8-32 today, seasonal (it.wikipedia, Laguna di Venezia); c. 800 lower near the river mouths with the rivers still in the lagoon (estimate 5-30)

hazards.danger: Grounding at low water; channels marked only by poles and local knowledge (estimate)

hazards.where: Lido, Malamocco (Metamauco), Chioggia and lesser inlets
hazards.danger: Shallow bars with strong ebb streams; breaking in a sirocco or bora (estimate)

phenomena: Acqua alta: water rising over the islands' edges on a sirocco autumn day

Fish traps and salt pans
records.change_800_to_1066: The ducal seat moves from Metamauco to Rialto in 811 after Pepin's attack of 810 (en.wikipedia, Malamocco; Venice); Metamauco is drowned in 1116 (after the game). Floods 840 and 885 in the record (en.wikipedia, Acqua alta). The lagoon slowly fills with river silt; the great diversions are 15th-17th century.
records.then_vs_now: Rivers still in the lagoon, fresher and muddier; ground and sea level about 1 m (estimate) lower relative to each other than today, so the early islands stood higher above the water than Venice's paving does now; no Marghera, no dredged ship channels, no jetties.

records.name: Comaclum (Comacchio) and the early-medieval Po delta

tide.phaseNote: Slightly smaller than Venice (estimate).
tide.tidalLimit: The tide runs some km up the Po di Volano at low river flow (estimate)
tide.notes: Comacchio stood on sandy beach ridges ('dossi') among brackish lagoons near the coast, on the Po di Volano system (it.wikipedia, Comacchio).

river.name: Po di Volano (with the Padovetere) and the Po di Primaro
river.notes: Before 1152 the Po reached the sea further south, by the Primaro branch (it.wikipedia, Rotta di Ficarolo); the Primaro 'did not exist before the 8th century' (it.wikipedia, Valli di Comacchio), so c. 800 the flow was splitting between the Volano and the young Primaro. Discharges here are a share of the whole Po (mean 1,506 at Pontelagoscuro, it.wikipedia Po) and are estimates (guess: about half in the Volano branch near Comacchio).

waves.notes: Estimate.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: River outflow through the channels (estimate)
sea.notes: The great Valli di Comacchio (168 km2 of brackish water today) did not exist before the 15th century: in the 8th century only small freshwater marshes lay south of the Po di Volano; sea water spread after embankments failed in the 14th century (it.wikipedia, Valli di Comacchio). So c. 800 Comacchio's surroundings are river levees, beach ridges, small brackish lagoons and freshwater marsh, not today's open valli.

optics.colour: Khaki-brown river water, greener in the small lagoons, reed-fringed
optics.turbidityCause: Po silt; marsh organic matter

salinityPsu.note: Fresh in the channels, brackish toward the sea (estimate)

records.change_800_to_1066: Comacchio is the delta's only trading centre in the 7th-9th centuries with one of the Adriatic's strongest fleets; Liutprand's charter (c. 715-730) lets its merchants carry salt and eastern goods up the Po to Pavia (it.wikipedia, Comacchio); Venice burns it in 932 (levels_793.json to-date 932) and attacks it five times in the High Middle Ages (it.wikipedia). The Primaro takes more of the Po during the period (estimate).
records.then_vs_now: No Valli di Comacchio lagoon, no Ficarolo course (1152), the Po's mouths 20-40 km south of today's delta tip (estimate from it.wikipedia Rotta di Ficarolo and en.wikipedia Po).

tide.phaseNote: Not tidal above the delta.
tide.tidalLimit: Only in the delta channels (see comacchio_po_delta)
tide.notes: Upstream travel is towing and rowing against the current; downstream is drifting with it (estimate).

river.name: Po (Padus)
river.notes: Mean 1,506 m3/s at Pontelagoscuro (1923-2011), minimum 270, maximum 13,000 (it.wikipedia, Po); en.wikipedia gives 1,540 mean and a 145 m3/s drought low in June 2022. Autumn floods dominate (Piedmont and Lombard tributaries); spring snowmelt floods too (it.wikipedia). The valley's slope falls from 0.35 to 0.14 (en.wikipedia writes per cent; per mille, i.e. 0.35-0.14 m/km, is meant, derived from the Po's fall); widest 503 m (en.wikipedia). Width, depth, current, bank height and ice frequency are estimates. Navigation: Roman sources say navigable to Turin (en.wikipedia); the Comacchio salt trade went up it to Pavia (it.wikipedia, Comacchio).

optics.turbidityCause: Alpine and Apennine silt and sand

records.change_800_to_1066: The Po's lower course runs south by Ferrara to the Volano and Primaro; the Ficarolo breach of 1152 (after the game) turns it north (it.wikipedia). Levees are local and few in 800 (estimate); the MCA after 950 slightly reduces hard winters.
records.then_vs_now: No continuous embankments, no dams on the Alpine tributaries, no gravel mining: wider, shallower, more braided, more sediment, bigger seasonal swings (estimate).

river.notes: Mean 350 m3/s at the Po confluence; minimum 54; maximum 5,000 (it.wikipedia, Ticino). The page also gives 69 m3/s at the Lake Maggiore outlet, which looks wrong (the lake's outflow is of the order of 290 m3/s, knowledge); treat it as doubtful. Pavia was the terminal of medieval trade by the Ticino (it.wikipedia). Width, depth, current, gradient and ice are estimates.

records.then_vs_now: No Miorina dam at the lake outlet (1940s) nor the Naviglio canals (12th century onward): a freer seasonal regime (estimate).

records.name: The Aegean (open sea of O18)

tide.phaseNote: Very small (knowledge); the Euripus strait at Chalcis is the famous exception with its reversing current (knowledge, outside the routes).
tide.notes: Tideless for a ship.

waves.swellFrom: N-NE (the meltemi, mid-May to mid-September) and S (winter sirocco and lodos storms)
waves.notes: Estimate. Meltemi seas are short, steep and white-crested at 2-3 m among the islands; the etesian winds reach force 7-8, strongest in the afternoon, often dying at night, sometimes days without a break; they come up in clear weather without warning (en.wikipedia, Etesian/Meltemi).

sea.notes: Maximum depth 2,639 m west of Karpathos (en.wikipedia). The meltemi blows NE-N in the north, N in the centre, NW in the south (en.wikipedia). A northbound sailing ship makes slow work of the summer: Philip II timed operations knowing southern fleets could not come north against it (en.wikipedia).

records.name: The Dardanelles (the Hellespont)

tide.phaseNote: No tide worth the name; the current is density- and wind-driven.
tide.notes: A surface current runs from the Black Sea toward the Aegean, a saltier undercurrent the other way (en.wikipedia). Surface speed 1-3 knots, up to about 4-5 knots in the Narrows at Canakkale with a strong NE wind (knowledge, estimate, not on the fetched pages).

waves.swellFrom: NE (down the strait) or SW (up it, against the current: steep)
waves.notes: Estimate; the strait's axis is NE-SW, so winds along it have 60 km of fetch.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Surface outflow SW 1-3 kn (to 4-5 kn in the Narrows), counter-eddies along the shores; saltier undercurrent NE below 15-25 m (knowledge, estimate)
sea.notes: 61 km long, 1.2-6 km wide, mean depth 55 m, maximum 103 m (en.wikipedia). Ships under sail historically waited at anchor for ideal conditions before entering (en.wikipedia): the prevailing NE wind (poyraz in winter, the etesian in summer) and the current both oppose a ship bound for Constantinople, so it waits at Tenedos or in the strait's bays for a southerly (knowledge). A 6th-century law set customs at the strait (wine 6 folles plus 2 sextarii, etc., en.wikipedia), collected at Abydos (knowledge).

optics.colour: Blue-green, greener than the Aegean (Black Sea water at the surface)
optics.turbidityCause: Plankton carried from the Marmara and Black Sea (estimate)

salinityPsu.note: Two layers: fresher Black Sea-derived surface water (about 25-29) over Aegean water near 38 (knowledge, estimate)

hazards.name: The Narrows (Canakkale-Kilitbahir)
hazards.danger: Strongest current; with a NE gale a sailing ship cannot pass northbound (en.wikipedia; speed estimate)

hazards.name: Nara point eddies
hazards.danger: Eddies and counter-currents round the point (estimate)

Ships at anchor waiting for the wind at Tenedos and in the bays

records.then_vs_now: No bridge (1915 Canakkale Bridge, 2022, en.wikipedia), no modern traffic scheme; the water is the same.

records.name: The Bosporus and the Golden Horn at Konstantinoupolis

tide.phaseNote: No tide; the level difference between the Black Sea and the Marmara drives the current.
tide.notes: The surface current runs south from the Black Sea at 3-4 knots in ordinary conditions and up to 7 knots when the wind feeds it; strongest in the middle reaches, about 5 km/h southward from off Kandilli; the 'orkoz' counter-currents along the shores run the other way at times up to 6-7 knots, strong enough a few times a year to stop the ferries (tr.wikipedia, Istanbul Bogazi). The famous 'Seytan akintisi' (Devil's current) runs round Akintiburnu at Arnavutkoy (knowledge).

waves.swellFrom: NE (Black Sea swell enters at the northern mouth) and SW (lodos from the Marmara)
waves.notes: Estimate; inside the strait the waves are wind-against-current chop.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Surface outflow south 3-4 kn, to 7 kn with wind; deep inflow of Marmara water northward starting at 15-20 m and reaching 45 m where depth allows (tr.wikipedia); outflow about 16,000 m3/s, about 500 km3 a year, at salinity about 17 (en.wikipedia, Black Sea)
sea.notes: 31 km long, 700 m to 3,420 m wide, average depth 65 m, maximum 124 m (en.wikipedia; tr.wikipedia gives mean 60 m, deepest 110 m between Bebek and Kandilli). The Golden Horn is an estuary 7.5 km long, up to 750 m wide, to about 35 m deep at its mouth, fed by the Alibey and Kagithane streams; the Byzantine chain ran across its entrance to Galata (en.wikipedia, Golden Horn). In past hard winters ice broken off the Black Sea piled up in the Bosporus bays (tr.wikipedia); the winter of 763-764, when the Black Sea's edge froze and floes jammed the strait, is recorded by Theophanes (knowledge, not verified this session).

optics.colour: Dark blue-green and fast-moving in the strait; greener and calmer in the Golden Horn, browner at the head where the streams enter
optics.turbidityCause: Black Sea plankton (summer blooms); stream silt at the head of the Golden Horn (estimate)

salinityPsu.note: Black Sea surface water 17-18 at the surface, Marmara water 35-36 below (tr.wikipedia); the saltiest surface around Uskudar

hazards.name: Drift ice
hazards.where: the northern Bosporus in rare severe winters
hazards.danger: Floes from the Black Sea packing the bays (tr.wikipedia; frequency guess)

Poyraz (NE) cold bright days, lodos (SW) warm storms
Spring sea fog (estimate)
Dolphins and migrating bonito and bluefish (knowledge)
The Golden Horn's calm green water among hundreds of ships

records.then_vs_now: No bridges, tunnels or embankments; natural shores, Byzantine harbours (Neorion, Prosphorion) along the Golden Horn (knowledge).

records.name: The northern North Sea (open water, Tyne to Shetland to Norway)

tide.phaseNote: The tide runs anticlockwise round the North Sea's amphidromic points: HW comes later going south down the British coast (Lerwick, Wick, Aberdeen, Tyne, Whitby in that order); the Norwegian side near the Skagerrak amphidromy has almost none (estimate from the station table).
tide.notes: Rim stations, neap to spring range (verified, Wikipedia North Sea table): Lerwick 0.79-1.82 m, Aberdeen 2.01-3.76 m, North Shields 2.38-4.61 m. Mid-sea ranges about 1-2 m (estimate). Offshore streams under 1 kn (estimate) except round Orkney and Shetland.

waves.swellFrom: N and NW: Norwegian Sea and Atlantic swell enters between Shetland and Norway
waves.notes: Mean and 99% Hs are estimates (typical of northern North Sea platform statistics, not re-opened). The record used is the Draupner event of 1 Jan 1995: Hs about 12 m, one wave of 25.6 m with its crest 18.5 m above still water (verified). North of 58 N the sea is not fetch-limited from the north: storm seas there are Atlantic seas. Decision 4: render at full height.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Anticlockwise circulation: Atlantic water enters past Shetland and through the Fair Isle gap, runs south along Scotland; the outflow leaves north along Norway as the Norwegian Coastal Current, 0.2-1 m/s, strongest off western Norway (direction verified in Wikipedia North Sea; speeds estimate).
sea.notes: Plateau depths 90-150 m, the Norwegian Trench along Norway to 725 m (verified). Sea ice never forms in the open northern North Sea; the same c. 800.

optics.colour: slate blue-green in sun, dark grey-green under cloud; ink blue in Atlantic water near Shetland, greener in the Norwegian coastal water
optics.turbidityCause: spring and late-summer plankton blooms; little sediment offshore

salinityPsu.note: 34-35 g/l offshore (verified North Sea average); 31-33 in the Norwegian Coastal Current (estimate)

hazards.name: Stad (Stadlandet)
hazards.where: the headland at the O2/O8 seam, 62.2 N
hazards.danger: the open-sea rounding Norwegians most feared: no lee, steep confused seas where Atlantic swell meets the coastal current over shoaling ground; boats waited for weather (knowledge)

hazards.name: Jæren's open coast
hazards.danger: harbourless sand and boulder shore with breakers in westerlies; the reason the sheltered lead begins at Karmsund (estimate)

phenomena: long Atlantic swell under a short wind sea (two systems crossing)
whitecaps from force 4, foam streaks from force 7
sea fog (haar) mostly April-July when warm air crosses the cold sea (knowledge)
glassy calms under summer highs with a low swell still running
bioluminescence late summer and autumn
spindrift in winter gales; snow showers marching over the sea in northerlies
records.change_800_to_1066: Same sea. The Medieval Climate Anomaly warms surface water by a few tenths of a degree after ~950 (estimate from decision 17); Eldgjá 939-940 gives two or three hard years. Storminess: no medieval statistics; keep modern frequencies (weather_and_sea_state.md 1.2).
records.then_vs_now: No platforms, lanes or lights; the sea itself is the same. Fish, seabirds and whales far more plentiful (knowledge).

records.name: Holy Island Sands and the Northumbrian coast (Lindisfarne, Bamburgh, the Farnes)

tide.phaseNote: HW roughly Dover +4 to +4.5 h (estimate); the flats flood fast through the channels between island and shore.

Spring range taken from North Shields (2.38-4.61 m, verified) as 4.2 m (estimate). The modern road causeway is open from about 3 h after HW to 2 h before the next HW (verified). c. 800 there was no causeway: the crossing was on foot or by cart over the sand at low water, the line later marked by the Pilgrims' Way posts; Bede describes the place as an island twice a day and joined to the land twice a day (Historia Ecclesiastica III.3, knowledge).

waves.swellFrom: NE-E: North Sea swell after northerly gales
waves.notes: Estimates (open to the N and E). Inside the Sands the island's harbour (the Ouse) is a calm pool in westerlies.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: weak southward coastal drift (estimate)
sea.notes: Bamburgh's rock stands on the shore 6 km SE of Lindisfarne; the Farne Islands lie 2-7 km offshore with races between them (knowledge).

optics.turbidityCause: resuspended sand and mud over the flats; spring plankton

salinityPsu.note: slightly fresher inside the Sands from small burns (estimate)

records.name: The Tyne estuary and Jarrow Slake (Gyrwe)

tide.phaseNote: HW about Dover +4.5 h (estimate).

river.name: Tyne
river.notes: Mean 44.6 m3/s at Bywell (verified). The Tyne Improvement Commission deepened the river from 6 to 30 ft (1.8 to 9.1 m) after 1850, dredging 150 million tonnes (verified): c. 800 the channel had about 1.8 m at low water over shoals, with islands and bars. Width at HW 200-400 m off Jarrow, flood peak ~1,500 m3/s, low flow ~5 m3/s, current speeds for the tidal reach: all estimates.

optics.colour: brown-olive, peat-tinged water over grey mud; greener at the mouth on the flood

salinityPsu.note: fresh above Newcastle to 30+ at the mouth on the flood (estimate)

hazards.name: Tyne bar and Herd Sand
hazards.danger: breaking seas across the bar in NE-E gales; about 2 m at low water before dredging (from the verified 6 ft)

hazards.danger: rocks covered at half flood (knowledge)

the brown ebb plume meeting green sea water at a foam line

records.then_vs_now: Undredged and unembanked: islands and sands in mid-river, Jarrow Slake a wide tidal flat (now docks), no quays, no piers at the mouth (piers 1854-1895, knowledge).

tide.phaseNote: HW about Dover +5 h (estimate).

tide.notes: Spring highs 5.75-5.85 m (verified tide-forecast, Sep-Oct 2026); spring range about 4.7-5.0 m (estimate from the listed lows). The harbour dries at low water.

features: the narrow gap between the cliffs
river.notes: Mean 4.8 m3/s at Sleights, max 350 m3/s (verified); floods of 1828, 1880 and 1930 took the bridges (verified). A flashy moorland river with brown peaty spates. Width, depth, speeds: estimates.

Portmahomack sits in a sandy bay on the east coast but facing west (verified), i.e. on the firth side of Tarbat Ness, sheltered from the open North Sea.

tide.notes: Bodø reference: MHWS 2.866, MHWN 2.257, MSL 1.688, MLWN 1.119, MLWS 0.510 m; 100-year 4.094 m (verified). Measured currents: 6 kn in 2018-2019, ships at 10 kn unable to make headway; the head across the strait up to 0.4 m (verified no.wikipedia). Older figures: up to 5 m/s (1986), 3 m/s max (1997), 1.7 m/s (1999 ship) (verified en.wikipedia). Strongest at full and new moon, weakest at half moon (Petter Dass, verified) and around July-August (verified). Eddies form between flood and ebb as the stream turns (verified).

waves.notes: Estimates. Ridge 40-60 m deep (verified no.wikipedia; en.wikipedia also says ~20 m), strait 7-8 km wide (verified). Atlantic swell against the stream over the ridge makes the danger; storm-driven flow adds to tide (verified).

records.name: The North Atlantic (Shetland - Faroes - Iceland - Greenland - Vinland)

tide.phaseNote: Open ocean: tide irrelevant offshore; ranges at the landfalls run from ~0.5 m (Tórshavn) to ~4 m (Reykjavík, Nuuk) (verified per record).

waves.swellFrom: W-SW: the stormiest swell field on Earth in winter
waves.notes: Mean and 99% Hs are estimates (winter means 4-5 m west of the Faroes, summer 1.5-2 m). Record: RRS Discovery in the Rockall Trough (2000) measured Hs up to 18.5 m and individual waves to 29.1 m (verified). A WMO-recognised 19 m Hs buoy record in this sea in Feb 2013 (knowledge, not re-opened). Decision 4: full height.

sea.nonTidalCurrent: The North Atlantic Current runs NE between Iceland and Scotland; the Irminger Current round west Iceland; the cold East Greenland Current south along Greenland at 6-12 cm/s annual mean, 20-30 cm/s at most, carrying more than 90% of the Arctic's exported sea ice (verified); the Labrador Current south past Newfoundland (knowledge).
sea.notes: Sea ice: the East Greenland drift ice (storis) lies along East Greenland all year and rounds Cape Farewell in late winter-summer (knowledge); Ice reaches north Iceland in heavy-ice years (Flóki saw Ísafjörður full of drift ice, verified saga). The Norse route kept well south of Iceland's south coast and well off East Greenland's ice (knowledge: the sailing directions of Landnámabók).

records.name: The southern North Sea (open water)

tide.phaseNote: The tide runs anticlockwise round amphidromic points in the Southern Bight and the German Bight: high water comes later going north up the Dutch coast and later again into the German Bight, while the English side runs south. Springs come about two days after new and full moon. Mid-Bight ranges are small; they grow to 4-6 m on the English side and toward the Strait of Dover.
tide.notes: Open-water ranges interpolated (estimate) between Hoek van Holland 1.69 m, Den Helder 1.37 m, Vlissingen 3.82 m mean (verified) and Dover c. 6 m springs (knowledge). Streams 1-2 kn along the axis, 2-3 kn toward the Strait (knowledge). c. 800: the same regime; a sea 0.5-1 m lower changes little offshore (estimate).

waves.swellFrom: N to NNW (Norwegian Sea storms), 10-14 s and low; westerly ocean swell is cut off by Britain, so this is mostly a short, steep wind sea
waves.notes: Mean, 99% and record Hs are knowledge-level values for the K13 / Europlatform area, not opened this session (estimate, low confidence). Use the wind-to-wave laws of weather_and_sea_state.md 1.3/2.4 (SPM fetch law in the adjusted wind, depth cap Hs <= 0.5 h). Decision 4 (full real height): a NW force 10 over the 500-600 km northerly fetch gives Hs 6-8 m in 30-40 m of water. Chronicle storms: 799, 838, 1014 (weather doc 1.2).

sea.nonTidalCurrent: Residual drift NE along the Dutch and German coasts (a few cm/s, more in SW winds) carrying the Rhine plume north; weak S-going drift down the English coast; wind drift 3% of U10 on top (weather doc 2.4).
sea.notes: No sea ice on the open water even in the 821/822 or 939-942 winters (estimate: the 1963 winter froze only the Wadden and harbour edges). Sandbanks rise to 5-15 m below the surface across much of the Bight; steep, breaking seas over them in gales.

optics.colour: Grey-green to bottle-green under cloud, slate-blue only in sun far offshore; never tropical blue. Whitecaps cream-white. The April-May plankton bloom turns it olive and leaves foam windrows.
optics.turbidityCause: Fine sand and silt resuspended in a shallow, tide-stirred sea; spring plankton bloom

records.then_vs_now: No wind farms, platforms, buoys or traffic lanes; the same colour of water. Far more fish (cod, herring, sturgeon), porpoise and grey whale (present until the 17th century, knowledge); oyster reefs on the banks that 19th-20th century dredging removed (knowledge), so locally a rougher bed and possibly clearer water over the reefs (guess).
